# Decisions D-500–D-749

Part of [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md), which lists every part. Entries keep their order; this part holds the numbers D-500–D-749.

<!-- entries -->
- **D-544 (2026-10-14, GUI "Dev run" mode; user feature request relayed by the orchestrator session; proposed
  defaults, every one editable; build: import side in G2, live side with G3).** A dev run imports **a few samples of
  every chosen corpus part** into fresh scratch corpora, then checks them, so a developer sees in minutes whether the
  pipeline still works end to end. Specification: `docs/reports/gui/design.md` §19.
  - **Import dev run (G2):** per source and part, N executions (default **5**), selected deterministically. With
    today's CLI the mode is **first-N** (`import --limit N`, the importer's own deterministic order); **spread**
    (round-robin over arms or variants) and **random with a recorded seed** need a core flag (a core need routed to the
    CLI robustness session: `import --sample N --sample-mode first|spread|random --seed S`), and the GUI offers them
    only when the CLI's `--help` lists that flag. Dev mode only: never `--release`, never `package`, `verify --release`
    or a deposit. Output: `$AGENTPROV_HOME/dev-runs/<UTC timestamp>/<corpus>/`, never a stored corpus. Steps per part:
    `import <source> --snapshot <part> --fetch --limit N` (offline fetch-cache read), `validate --corpus` (every tier; the scratch corpus
    is small), `recompute --corpus --dry-run`; one summary row per part (mapped, degenerate, issues, validation, recompute
    differences, timing). Every step runs through `tools/suite_queue.py --class import --cpu 2` (a small reservation, so
    a dev run never starves a gate). The last **5** dev runs are kept; older `dev-runs/<timestamp>` folders are deleted
    automatically, and only those folders, never while a job of the run is running.
  - **Live capture dev run (designed now, built with G3):** transport **scripted** by default (`--llm-script`; no
    network, no API call, no cost); 3 tasks per suite, 1 attack per task, all configured suites. A real-model dev run is
    opt-in: the §8.3 estimate first, explicit consent, a hard cap of **5** model calls in total (editable), keys only from
    the keychain through `run --env-stdin` (D-395), never a dotenv file.
  - **Settings › Dev runs:** the default N; a per-source/part override table; include and exclude lists; sampling mode
    and seed; keep count; queue CPU reservation; for live: transport, tasks per suite, suites, attacks per task, call cap
    and cost cap. Stored in the GUI's settings; "Reset to defaults" restores the shipped values.
  - **Caveat (core review D, CD-7):** with `--limit`, the raw members stored can depend on the import batch size. The
    fix is held in a core branch; today's `import` has no `--batch-size` option to pin, so a dev run records the CLI
    commit and treats sampled raw-member sets as non-comparable across CLI versions until the fix lands.
  - **Rejected:** dev runs into the stored corpora (they are read-only for the GUI and a sample would corrupt their
    identity); sampling in the GUI by building `--select` filters per arm (it needs the arms, which only the reader
    knows, and duplicates core logic); unbounded retention.
  - **Downstream:** GUI only (`gui/`, design §19); one core need (the sampling flag) routed to the orchestrator. No AER,
    SEM or PROV byte, corpus or core module changes.
- **D-545 (2026-10-14, GUI S11 tolerance for psutil's `socket` import; user decision 2026-10-15: approved; amends D-396 S11 like D-448).**
  `psutil` (design §2.2, D-392: job identity and the System tab) imports `socket` at module level for its
  address-family constants; it opens no socket. The fresh-interpreter S11 check therefore tolerates `socket` and
  `_socket` **only when their importer is `psutil`** (checked with an import hook in the test); the static bans in
  `gui/src` stay, and `ssl`, `http.client`, `urllib.request`, `asyncio`, `QtNetwork` and web views stay forbidden.
  - **Rejected:** dropping psutil (the pid-plus-create-time identity and the sampler need it, and re-implementing them
    per OS is larger and riskier); importing psutil lazily (the job manager needs it at start for re-attach).
- **D-600 (2026-10-21, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, pre-check PC-redcode-exec-openhands-01/02,
  PC-autogen-guard-placement-01, CC-13: native secret-shape rules in the release scan; user decision 2026-10-21:
  approved, class 0).**
  - **Context:** gitleaks is the release scan's one secret scanner (G.9.4), and it runs at `--max-archive-depth 0`
    (D-450), because its own extraction is not bounded by the G.3 limits. So it never reads an archive member. The
    path scan reads members decoded (D-491), but until now it searched them only for the home path, the host name and
    account paths (D-457). The corpus pre-check of 2026-10-21 found a Hugging Face token shape in one member of
    redcode-exec-openhands's supplementary zip (PC-01; the batch never opened that zip, PC-02) and a Langfuse key pair
    in one not-selected member of the autogen-guard-placement deposit zip (PC-01). The release scan would have passed
    both with no finding.
  - **Decision:**
    - The path scan (`tools/release_scan.py`) gains native secret-shape rules (`SECRET_SHAPES`), applied to every file
      it reads and to every decoded archive member through the D-491 `member_scan` hook. They use the same locators and
      the same fail-closed `home-path-unscanned` finding as the other path-scan rules.
    - Rule ids are gitleaks 8.30.1's own where it has the rule, so a `[withhold]` policy's `scan_rules` and the builder
      backstop (D-236) name one id for both detectors:
      - `github-pat` (`ghp_`), `github-oauth` (`gho_`), `github-app-token` (`ghu_` and `ghs_`) and
        `github-refresh-token` (`ghr_`), each followed by 36 of `[0-9A-Za-z]`;
      - `github-fine-grained-pat` (`github_pat_` and 82 of `[0-9A-Za-z_]`);
      - `huggingface-access-token` (`hf_` and 34 of `[A-Za-z0-9]`; gitleaks' rule takes letters only and needs a
        terminator, so the native rule is the wider of the two).
      gitleaks has no Langfuse rule, so two ids are AgentPROV's: `langfuse-secret-key` and `langfuse-public-key`
      (`sk-lf-` or `pk-lf-` followed by a UUID, 8-4-4-4-12 hex digits, either case).
    - Boundaries: a shape must not follow a letter, digit or `_`, and must not be followed by a character of its own
      body. A longer token that holds a shape is not a hit.
    - The D-457 route: a literal is found with a plain byte search, then the shape is matched anchored there. Every part
      has a fixed length, so a match is bounded (`_SECRET_SPAN` = 100 bytes, which the chunk carry covers) and never
      backtracks. A shape is judged only when the byte after it is in the window, so a token cut at a chunk boundary
      is judged in the next window. The end of the file is the last bytes once more with a NUL after them, as in D-457.
    - No entropy threshold applies (gitleaks uses one): a low-entropy shape is a finding, to be triaged.
    - A finding records no value: path, rule and line only, fingerprint `<path>:<rule>:<line>`. It is untriaged and
      goes through the existing triage values (`real`, `synthetic-benchmark`, `false-positive`; no new value, so
      `agentprov.release` is unchanged).
    - A native finding whose fingerprint gitleaks also reported (a token in a stored file, same rule id, same line) is
      dropped (`native_findings`), so nothing is reported twice. A member finding (`<path>#<locator>`) never collides.
    - `PATH_SCAN_VERSION` becomes 4.
  - **Census** (count-only script, members read in memory, no value or member name printed). The rules were run over
    the pinned snapshots:
    - redcode-exec-openhands's `agent-execution-decisions-supp.zip`: 3,397 file members; 1 member with
      `huggingface-access-token` on 2 lines (PC-01's two `export` lines); no other shape.
    - Its six trajectory zips: 5,460 file members; 0 hits.
    - autogen-guard-placement's deposit zip: 109 file members; 1 member with `langfuse-secret-key` and
      `langfuse-public-key`, one line each. The synthetic sk-shaped string beside them, with its impossible key
      length, is not a hit.
    - No GitHub shape anywhere.
    The withholding itself is D-602 and D-603.
  - **Rejected:**
    - raising gitleaks' `--max-archive-depth`: its extraction is not bounded by the G.3 limits (D-450), and it reads
      to disk;
    - a second scanner (trufflehog was dropped, AD-10 row 19);
    - AgentPROV-own ids for the GitHub and Hugging Face shapes: a policy would then need two ids for one secret;
    - one combined `github-pat` id for every GitHub prefix: gitleaks names them separately, and its findings on stored
      files would then not deduplicate against the native ones;
    - native rules on archive members only: a member and its stored copy (a selected member) would then be scanned
      differently.
  - Byte class 0 (`tools/` and docs). No corpus byte changes. A scan document written afterwards records path scan
    version 4 and may hold new untriaged findings, so triage files for corpora that hold such shapes need review.
- **D-604 (2026-10-21, bug pass bugpass-perf-10: third-party account paths inside content; principle; user decision
  2026-10-21: approved, tool output only).**
  - **Context:** D-182 redacts workstation account paths in harness-written fields only. Its rejected alternatives
    (`docs/reports/phase10h/redaction-design.md` §8) keep model output and benchmark content verbatim. D-186 (c) ships
    raw objects as they are, because they are public at the pin. The pre-check of 2026-10-21 found third-party account
    paths inside execution content: tool and environment output (a shell's working directory, a traceback, a listing)
    in whistlebench, credleak, openagentsafety and agentops. Model-authored text can repeat such a path. D-457 makes
    the release scan report them. They cannot be released without either withholding whole executions or editing
    evidence.
  - **Decision (principle; the family branches apply it: D-601 whistlebench, D-605 credleak, D-606 openagentsafety,
    D-608 agentops. D-607, dtap, is a decision of its own: a structural pattern limited to a profile `labels`
    allowlist of salted labels, over every AER string):**
    1. A third-party account path inside **tool or environment output** is redacted in the derived records (AER, SEM,
       PROV) as D-182 redacts harness fields. A salted label stands in its place. The pointer is tagged `D` and cites
       the family's versioned redaction rule. An info issue is sealed. The original, or a digest of it, is never
       recorded.
    2. **Model-authored text stays verbatim.** A path the model wrote (an assistant message, a tool call's arguments)
       is never redacted: that would falsify what the model did.
    3. The **raw objects** that hold the path are withheld at **object scope** (D-235, `personal_data`). Their
       executions stay released, and `WITHHELD.json` keeps their pinned origins and stage digests.
    4. An **execution whose derived record still holds the path** (because the model wrote it) is withheld at
       execution scope through D-235.
    5. It departs from D-182 §8 ("never redact benchmark content") and from D-186 (c) for these sources only. Every
       other source keeps D-182 and D-186 as they are.
    6. **The label's limit (user decision 2026-10-21: keep the deterministic `{span12}`, disclose the limit).** A label
       is a 12-hex digest of the span salted with the public profile id, so a short or common name can be recovered by
       guessing candidates. It hides the name from a reader, not from someone who guesses. The datasheet states this
       (statement `redaction-labels-guessable`), and so does the release decision (G.9.6). The release scan does not
       report a label as an account (`acct-<12 hex>`, `REDACTION_LABEL` in `tools/release_scan.py`).
    7. **Raw residue ships as pinned (user decision 2026-10-21).** Where a raw file still holds a third-party account
       in a form no exact withhold rule can target (byte patterns cannot use the labels, so a broad rule would also
       catch other names and, through D-235, withhold executions whose derived records keep benchmark names), the raw
       file ships as pinned (D-186 (c)); its derived records are redacted; the corpus's datasheet discloses it. The
       release scan's `account-path` findings on such files are triaged `pinned-account`, which the deposit builder
       accepts for an `account-path` finding in `raw/` only (`release.refused.scan_pinned` anywhere else, since a
       derived record must be redacted). Applies to credleak's raw cells (bare name), DTap's raw trajectories,
       WhistleBench's raw samples and openagentsafety's raw trajectories and state files. Item 3 (object-scope
       withholding) still applies where an exact structural rule exists (interbolt D-456, D-608, D-609, fragfuse,
       kexin). EnvironmentOptim's raw logs ship as pinned under D-510 (user decision 2026-10-21).
  - **Consequences:**
    - The redacted records differ from a verbatim mapping. Each redaction is visible (a `D` pointer, the rule id, the
      info issue), so the AER still says what was observed and what a rule changed (invariant 2).
    - The family's adapter or profile digest moves, so each family branch is a class-1 regeneration item with its own
      byte-impact table.
    - Released executions recompute only from the withheld raw's pinned origin, which `WITHHELD.json` names (D-230).
    - The datasheet discloses the redaction, the withheld objects and the withheld executions.
    - The release scan's `account-path` findings on withheld objects are covered by `WITHHELD.json`. Findings on
      released derived records must be 0 for the target accounts (the residue each family census records).
  - **Rejected:**
    - **Full content redaction** (redact model-authored text too). It edits the record of what the model said and
      did, which is the evidence the corpus exists for, and it breaks the D-182 rule that model output is never
      redacted.
    - **No content redaction, withholding the executions instead.** Every execution whose tool output holds a path
      would be withheld. For these sources that can be a large share of their executions, lost for a path that a
      label can stand in for without loss to any analysis of agent behaviour.
    - **Shipping as is (D-186 (c) extended to derived records).** It publishes third-party account names in
      AgentPROV's own records, which D-457 and the user decision of 2026-10-15 rule out.
  - Byte class 0 for this entry (a principle). Each applying branch records its own byte impact.

- **D-603 (2026-10-21, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, pre-check PC-01: `autogen-guard-placement` withholds the deposit zip
  that holds a real-format service secret key; user decision 2026-10-21: approved, object-scope withhold of the zip, 0
  executions).**
  - **Context:** one member of the pinned deposit zip (Zenodo 23025259 v1.0), `results/phase7/capture.json`, holds a
    secret key of the study's own observability service (Langfuse shape: `sk-lf-` and a UUID) in its rail
    configuration. The profile selects neither it nor any capture outside phase 0, so the corpus stores it only inside
    the deflated zip: no stored object holds the key's bytes literally, and the zip would be released with it. The
    pre-check could not establish that the key is synthetic (CC-13: a real-format secret of the source's own
    infrastructure, S0).
  - **Decision:** profile version 2 gains `[withhold]`, reason `secret`, one bounded pattern rule `langfuse-secret-key`
    (the prefix and a lower-case hex UUID, 42 bytes) at scope `object`. At seal, the decoded scan of D-450 reads the
    zip's unstored members and withholds the zip object only (basis `profile_rule`, detector
    `agentprov-withhold-decoded/1`, no affected execution); its 43 selected members, stored as objects of their own,
    and every execution stay released. `WITHHELD.json` names the rule id, never a match. `scan_rules` is left out until
    the release-scan rule of D-600 for this shape is on main (follow-up: add its id then, a byte change of the profile
    and so a D-31 bump if a corpus records v2).
  - **Census (exact rule over the real pinned zip, members decoded in memory, and over the pre-check corpus
    `l2-v1.0-j2`):** 1 of 109 members matches (the target, not selected, deflated); 0 of 14 primary run files (11 with
    runs, 3 with rows only), 0 of 29 stored context and auxiliary objects, 0 in the zip's stored bytes, 0 of 1,080 AER,
    1,080 SEM and 1,080 PROV files. The product backstop (`withhold.rescan`, D-450 decoded scan) over all 3,290 files of
    that corpus reports exactly one hit, the zip object, and no unscanned archive. Executions withheld: 0 of 1,080.
  - **D-31:** v2 with v1 archived (scratch corpora record v1, see the D-31 addendum of 2026-10-21, D-603). Byte class 1:
    the AER header's profile version and `profile_sha256` move for every autogen AER (1,080); SEM and PROV follow
    through `aer_digest`; no committed AER pin of this family exists, so none is re-pinned. No stored corpus records the
    profile. Regen-batch item 142; held branch `bugpass-regen-d603`. D-31 owner approved the bump 2026-10-21. The older
    recorded version-1 digest `56b86c1131fd…` (the profile of `d9e1d5a2`) was superseded by D-321's in-place edit
    (`3015cf7a`, 2026-10-14) before D-31's strict rule was applied on main (item 30, `ee2f286e`), so it is not archived;
    the phase-10n partials recording it (`autogen-j3`, `autogen-j8`) must never be sealed.
  - **Tests:** `tests/adapters/autogen/test_withhold_e2e.py` imports a synthetic deposit zip (the committed fixture
    members and one unselected member at the PC-01 label holding a test-made key of the shape, assembled at run time) in
    release mode with the shipped profile, seals it and runs `verify --level chain --release`: the zip is withheld
    (`profile_rule`, decoded detector, no execution), the 20 executions and every selected member are released, no
    sealed or deposited byte holds the key (stored or decoded), the sidecar does. It fails on the v1 profile (the zip is
    released with the key).
  - **Rejected:** allowlisting the key as localhost-only (PC-01's other option: the key's validity cannot be checked
    without testing it, which is never done, and a real-format secret is not released); withholding by the member's
    label or the zip's digest (D-454 (ii) rejected identity rules); a release-scan finding alone (the scan reports, it
    does not withhold, H.4.5); selecting the member so that its object is withheld instead (it is not evidence of any
    run).
  - **Not done:** the artefact-catalogue entry PC-01 proposed (`autogen.art.rail_config_key_shapes`). An entry needs a
    detector rule in the `autogen` catalogue; adding one changes the catalogue's bytes (a D-31 bump to `autogen@2`) and
    the rules every AER declares, for a case no AER field shows. Routed to the family owner with the round.

- **D-605 (2026-10-21, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, pre-check PC-01/PC-02 (credleak-p15b); user decision 2026-10-21:
  approved, apply D-604 (tool output only); second user decision 2026-10-21: the generic structural `[withhold]` rule
  (part 1) and a labelled `ls -l` owner/group rule (part 2)).**
  - **Context:** the credleak deposit's tool output holds one named workstation account (account #1; the name is never
    recorded) in `home/<account>/` paths of 313 runs in 67 cells (319 runs in 68 cells counting the bare path). Raw
    pointers: `turns/*/toolCalls/*/output` 382 strings, model-authored `input/command` 38, `input/file_path` 1,
    `assistantResponse` 4. The canary and key rules withhold 176 of the 313 runs (182 of the 319). 137 runs and 18 cells holding the path
    would be released, and the family had no redaction mechanism. D-604 (principle): redact such paths in tool and
    environment output only, keep model-authored text verbatim, withhold raw objects holding the path at object scope,
    and withhold through D-235 an execution whose derived files still hold it.
  - **Decision (built, regen-batch item 138, spec D.19.15):**
    - `adapters/credleak/redact.py` is a family copy of the D-476 grammar (no cross-family import). It reads a closed
      table `[[family.credleak.redact]]` `{id, scope, pattern, replacement, leaf?, note?}` whose one scope is
      `tool_output`: the `output` of a `toolCalls[]` entry, which the mapper copies into the tool result message.
    - The redaction runs on the source value before encoding, so every AER copy is the label: the string, member names,
      the `ext.lex` order lists and pointers, and `$utf16`-wrapped strings. This is the BF-21 property, by construction.
    - Each redacted pointer is tagged `D` and cites `credleak.value_redacted@1` (new, class D) scoped to it.
      `ext.credleak.redacted` lists `{p, rule: "<profile>@<version>#<rule id>"}`, and the info issue
      `credleak.value_redacted` counts the pointers. Source locators keep naming the raw field.
    - The profile rule `account_path` is path-anchored: `home/` or `Users/`, with or without a leading slash, not after a
      name character. A negative look-ahead skips release_scan's `ACCOUNT_ALLOWLIST` names within the name class (29,
      case-insensitive, trailing dots ignored; a test keeps the lists equal) and dots-only names. The name is 1 to 64 name
      characters ending at the first character that cannot be part of a name.
    - The replacement is `acct-{span12}`: the span is the name, and the salt is the profile id.
    - The mapper wires it in (`_Build._call`; the count and issue come in a post-step of `run`). Model-authored text
      (tool-call input, assistant text) and the scripted user message are never rewritten.
  - **Census** (pinned v3 zip, sha256 `7e5f7e40…`, in memory; the 68 cells holding the path mapped by the shipped
    mapper and profile 2; counts only):
    - 382 pointers are redacted in 316 runs, and the pattern matches 396 tool-output strings over all 643 cells;
    - **residue: 0 runs hold account #1 in path form in a tool result**;
    - 19 runs in 8 cells keep it in model-authored fields: `args.command` 38 and `args.file_path` 1 (message and
      `tool_execution`, so also PROV `apv:args` in all 19), and assistant text 4. 17 of the 19 are already withheld by
      the canary and key rules;
    - 0 degenerate runs, and no committed fixture run holds a non-generic path in tool output (the `ls -l` rule of part
      2 touches 12 of the 124 fixture runs, below).
  - **Part 2: the bare name in `ls -l` columns (built).** Account #1 also appears without a path, as the owner and group
    columns of `ls -l` lines in tool output. Two labelled rules handle it (the D-607 approach), `ls_long_owner` and
    `ls_long_group`:
    - each has a structural pattern: a mode string, a link count, then the owner (and, for the group rule, the group)
      as the `span` group;
    - each lists `labels = ["86fe70f091cd"]`, account #1's salted `{span12}`. A one-off `python3 -I` script computed it
      from the pinned data and printed only the label. The name is written nowhere, and the label is the one the path
      rule already writes into the AER;
    - a labelled rule replaces only its span, and only when the span's label is listed (grammar addition `labels?`,
      `family.schema.json`); tool output only (D-604).

    Census, the shipped Redactor over every tool output of the 643 cells, as the mapper applies it:
    - **22,986 owner and 22,985 group columns of account #1 in 4,353 runs are redacted; residue 0 in `ls -l` columns**;
    - **collateral 0**: 5,757 `ls -l` lines of other owners are left as they are;
    - runs holding the bare token in tool output go from 4,432 to 29. The 29 hold it in 30 lines that are not `ls -l`
      lines (other command output), which no rule covers;
    - 92 raw cells hold the bare token and are released by the policy. D-604 withholds raw objects for the path only,
      so their raw tool output keeps the `ls -l` columns.
    - The 124 committed fixture runs include 12 whose `ls -l` columns are redacted (13 pointers): **the committed
      credleak fixtures (`tests/fixtures/credleak/`, unedited deposit cells) hold account #1's bare name in Git.**
  - **D-31:**
    - Profile `credleak-p15b` 1 → 2. The archived v1 is `1dce158a57ad…` (pinned in `tests/unit/test_d31_bumps.py`): the
      bytes of 4 scratch corpora (phase10k `trial/c2.partial`, `trial/c2seal`, precheck `l2-head-j1/j2.partial`) and
      of the gui-build sealed copy `~/.agentprov/migration-work/gui-build/pkg/credleak-p15b`.
    - 10 older scratch corpora (phase10k `trial/old*/`) record earlier version-1 bytes `c5977363f485…`,
      `db30e9ee6c04…` and `e9f62b26d2da…`, with catalogue bytes `922175558bb4…` and `3235c52ce785…` and semantics bytes
      `7e1ab56243ae…`. They are not archived: per the F-8 ruling they are reproduced at their building commit.
    - Catalogue `credleak` 1 → 2: rule and issue code added; v1 `d355a2725e17…` archived and pinned.
    - Semantics `credleak.tools` gains version 2 (version 1's tables, declaring catalogue 2, H.2.5; `CATALOGUE_OF`).
      Version 1 (`721620e801f2…`) is unchanged. The registry selects `credleak.tools@2`.
    - **The sealed v1 copies (phase10k `trial/c2seal`, `trial/old*/c2seal`, the gui-build sealed copy) and the deposit
      bundle `~/.agentprov/migration-work/gui-build/pkg/deposit` were built before this redaction. They may hold
      account #1 in released files and must never be deposited.**
  - **Part 1: withholding (built; user decision 2026-10-21: the generic structural rule).** Two object-scope pattern
    rules in `[withhold]`, `account-path-home` (`home/[A-Za-z0-9._]{1,64}[^A-Za-z0-9._\-]`) and `account-path-users`
    (the same after `Users/`), each with `reason = "personal_data"` and its own `public_note`. The table keeps `secret`
    (parse_policy allows a reason per rule).
    - The byte grammar has no alternation or look-around, so the rules cannot exclude generic names. They write nothing
      about the account into Git.
    - The name class leaves out `-`, so the redaction labels `acct-<12 hex>` never match (tested).
    - A raw cell holding such a path is withheld at object scope. A derived file that still holds one holds it in
      model-authored text, because the tool-output copies are redacted, and withholds its execution (D-235).

    Census with the shipped policy (`scan_chunks` over every raw cell, and over the AER, SEM and PROV of all 2,740 runs
    of the 80 cells that can hit the rules), beyond the 5,422 executions the four existing rules withhold:
    - **7 executions newly withheld**: 2 of account #1's model-authored residue, 3 with another non-generic account
      path in model-authored text, and **2 with a generic-name path only**. Those 2 are a known collateral cost the
      user accepted (2026-10-21);
    - **21 raw cells newly withheld**: 18 holding account #1, 3 other;
    - 28 executions the existing rules withhold also hit the new rules.

    Options that were measured and not chosen:
    - account #1's length-and-class shape: 4 new executions and 20 cells, but it writes the name's length and classes
      into Git;
    - `/home/[A-Za-z0-9._\-]{1,64}/`: 142 new executions, because it matches the labels;

    The release scan's `account-path` finding of the `/home/acct-<12 hex>/` labels is class 0 in `tools/` and is handled

- **D-500 (2026-10-14, core review A finding CA-21; user decision 2026-10-14: option 1; held for the regeneration
  round as regen item 85).** An asserted null goes on `apv:<prop>Status`, never on the data property.
  - **Problem.** E.5 item 5 turned an asserted JSON null into the QName `apv:RecordedNull`, and the engine wrote that IRI
    as the object of `owl:DatatypeProperty` terms with `rdfs:range xsd:string` (`apv:error`, `apv:taskId`,
    `apv:defenceId` and every attribute written through `opt()`/`lit()`). That is not OWL 2 DL, and under RDFS it entails
    `apv:RecordedNull a xsd:string` (`docs/reports/review-core-a/repro/CA-21_A3-1`).
  - **Rule.** For every such data property, `apv:<prop>Status` (an object property with range `apv:EpistemicStatus`,
    following `apv:contentStatus`, E.4.5) carries `apv:RecordedNull`, and the data property is omitted. Five status
    properties already existed (`finishReasonStatus`, `requestedModelStatus`, `servedModelStatus`,
    `providerCallIdStatus`, `indexStatus`); 26 are new. Together with D-501 this is apv **0.2.0**, a minor bump under
    E.4.6 item 2 (terms added, none changed or removed). `vocab/apv-0.2.ttl` declares `owl:priorVersion` and
    `owl:backwardCompatibleWith` 0.1.0; `docs/ns/apv-0.1.ttl` stays published.

    24, nothing is released and every PROV document is regenerated in the round; the catalogue's `vocabulary` is
    0.2.0. `corpus.json` `ontology.version` is a closed const in `agentprov-corpus/0.1`, so apv 0.2.0 rides with
    `agentprov-corpus/0.2` (deferrals part C), whose shape and writer carry 0.2.0 per format. Items 85/86 land in the
    same pre-round integration as part C, immediately before it, so that no corpus is sealed in between.
  - **Rejected:** weakening the ranges to `rdf:Property` (a change of meaning, so apv 1.0.0, and OWL typing lost);
    documenting the violation and keeping it (vocabulary and documents contradicting each other, which E.4.6 item 2

  - **Objects absent on purpose (BF-20, CB-6).** A raw object that `purge` removed (`raw/tombstones.jsonl`), that a sealed
    corpus withholds (`WITHHELD.json`) or that it only references (`raw/REFERENCES.json`) is counted
    (`<kind>_unavailable`), not refused with `raw.object.missing`. The executions that need such an object, directly or
    through a container (AD-12), are not re-mapped, and `recompute` and `verify --level rederive` classify them

    accepts an included object the derivation accounts for (`CorpusWriter.absent_ok`). Any other absence still refuses.
  - **Resume key (BF-32).** `derived_from` also records `semantics` and the `fn_digests` of the recomputed layers, so a

    sealed corpus as `rederive.index_refreshed`: failed, or unverified when a declared version differs. The

    in a re-derive (seal needs it to build `WITHHELD.json`).

    - Working manifests that use context trees gain `snapshot.context[]` fields. Sealed corpus-0.1 manifests carry none.

- **D-550 (2026-10-14, tier-4 round-trip cache; session prov-perf; requested by the user; push approved by the user in
  the prov-perf window, 2026-10-14).** The
  PROV-O round trip of tier 4 (the `pv.roundtrip.*` checks; 65–81% of pipeline CPU) is kept under
  `$AGENTPROV_HOME/cache/tier4` (`validate/cache.py`), so a document whose bytes and context are unchanged is not
  round-tripped again.
  - **Key.** The document's sha256 plus the context: the sha256 of every `agentprov` source file (which subsumes the
    validation stage digest), the version and code-file digest of `prov`, `rdflib`, `pyparsing`, `isodate`, `lxml`,
    `python-dateutil` and `six`, the Python build, and the round-trip options.
  - **Value.** The five outcomes exactly as returned, with their digest. A completed round trip only: never `skipped`,
    never `pv.roundtrip.load`.
  - **Rules.**
    - A bad entry is a miss and is removed.
    - Writes are atomic renames, and size is bounded by LRU eviction.
    - T1 jobs get a prefetched hint and return a frame; the parent does all I/O (G.4.4).
    - `validate_prov(..., fidelity=)` consults the cache only inside `if roundtrip:`, so the G2c-5 skip
      (`--skip-prov-conformance`) composes: a skipped run never reads or writes an entry.
    - `--no-validation-cache` turns it off.
    - `validate --release` never reads an entry: it recomputes and audits the entries it finds.
  - **Rejected.**
    - Caching all of tier 4: the key would need the AER, SEM and catalogue digests, and the rest is cheap.
    - A key built from the validation digest alone: the round trip also runs `prov/serialise/nquads.py`, the strict
      loader and the vocabulary.
    - Library versions without file digests: a patched or forked library keeps its version string.
    - Letting T1 workers read the cache: the audit hook forbids it, and it would widen G.4.5.
    - SQLite: a corrupt database is harder to make a clean miss, and the user asked for atomic write-rename.
    - Trusting the binding for release: a forged local entry, or an unseen nondeterminism, would enter a decision that
      third parties rely on; one full release validation costs about 3 h.
  - **Downstream.** Class 1: `validate/` moves the validation stage's `engine_code_sha256` (regen-batch item 94).
    Later, `adapters/runner/provjob.py` and the importer move the AER engine digest, and they join item 94. No AER, SEM,
    PROV or validation-row bytes change. Reports: `docs/reports/prov-perf/cache-design.md`. Spec: N.2.5 item 9 and
    E.5.5 "Reuse".
- **D-551..D-556 (2026-10-14, PROV memory; session prov-perf; user decisions 2026-10-14, relayed by the orchestrator
  session).** The evidence is in `docs/reports/prov-perf/memory-profile.md`. Peak RSS ≈ 47 MiB + 82 MiB per PROV MiB
  (R² 0.999), and no stored-corpus document peaks above 0.4 GB. The 4 GiB per-job cap, not real memory, sets the M2's
  worker count at 6.
  - **D-551** (`gc.collect()` at the round trip's phase boundaries): **measured, not adopted** (user, 2026-10-14). Its
    CPU cost, +6% to +15% of tier 4 for four full collections, exceeds its value (peak −10% to −25%) once D-554 sizes
    the pool by evidence. Revisit only for jobs above a size threshold (long-run sources at 1–2 GB), and only if
    D-554's budget needs it.
  - **D-552** (model 1 from the parsed tree): **not adopted** (user, 2026-10-14): no measurable benefit (no peak change,
    about −1% CPU).
  - **D-553** (per-unit round trip; peak −49% to −60%): **deferred** (the user: peaks are already modest).
  - **D-554** (size the worker pool by predicted peak, or admit jobs by a memory budget, keeping the 4 GiB hard cap):
    **approved**, routed to pipeline-perf to build with D-415 after D-414 lands. It is the change that moves the round's
    time on the 32 GB machine (6 → 12 workers, about 1.6× in the CPU-bound phases).
  - **D-555** (`prov`/`rdflib` changes as a fork or upstream suggestions): **not proposed**.
  - **D-556** (the `collection` encoding, orjson/ijson, `gc.freeze`, oxrdflib): **rejected** as recorded in the report.
- **D-560 (2026-10-15, phase 10i follow-up; user decision 2026-10-15, relayed by the orchestrator and confirmed by the user in the phase-10i session): archive inputs register the members a profile `exclude` entry matches.**
  - **Problem.** The `expand` selection of an archive input is the profile's include globs only (R-40). A member that an
    `exclude` entry names is therefore a `not_selected` row of `raw/members.jsonl`, and it gets no register entry.
    The snapshot reports `selection_excluded: 0`. Found by the AgentOps-Bench trial: its 3,842 out-of-scope run files
    had no `select.out_of_scope` entries, so D-143/D-191 ("recorded as excluded") held only through the member rows.
  - **Decision.** The runner registers every `not_selected` member that matches an `exclude` entry, with that entry's
    code, owner and note, exactly as for a directory input. The snapshot's `selection_excluded` counts it, and D-191
    holds as written.
  - **Rejected:** accepting the member rows as the record and amending D-191 (it loses the per-file code that tells
    out-of-scope from not-an-execution); selecting excluded members only to register them (it decompresses data that
    is never used, against R-40).
  - **Affected:** every archive-input profile with `exclude` entries.
    - On main: `agentops-bench-pilot`, `credleak-p15b`, `code-agent-misalignment-geminicli`, `seagent-agentdojo`,
      `controlarena-persistent`.
    - From phase 10j: `authority-caps-agentdojo`, `ipi-defenses-agentdojo`, and `dca-agentdojo` if its url pin becomes
      an archive input.
  - **Downstream.** `adapters/runner/importer.py` is in the `aer` stage's `engine_code_sha256` (class 1). Those corpora
    gain register rows and `selection_excluded` counts at their next import. No AER, SEM or PROV byte changes. Regen
    item 100; held branch `phase-10i-context`; tests: AgentOps-Bench (3,842) and a directory-input control.
- **D-540 (2026-10-15, core review C finding CC-17; user decision 2026-10-15: approved, delegated to the orchestrator
  and confirmed directly by the user). `agentprov.api.check_claim` forwards every keyword of the claims library.**

    `phrase`. Through the facade a correct `agent_execution` value always gave `NC-ALL-13` and a correct
    `coverage_claim` always gave `NC-ALL-08`, so DoD Q.11b could not pass for them.
  - **Change.** `check_claim(source_ids, tags, *, derivation=None, location="", agent_executions_only=False,
    phrase=None)`, all forwarded; the M.6 and I.5.6 signature blocks match. Test: `tests/cli/test_api_check_claim.py`
    (the facade's keyword-only parameters and defaults equal the library's; the two calls above return `[]`).
  - **Rejected:** forwarding `**kwargs` unchecked (the facade would not document its contract).

- **D-541 (2026-10-15, core review C finding CC-16 follow-up; user decision 2026-10-15: approved, delegated to the
  orchestrator and confirmed directly by the user). `agentprov.api.rows(corpus, "lineage")` is built.**
  - **Rows (MN M.6; O.3.5 F5).** One row per edge, columns `from_node`, `to_node`, `relation`, `n`, `basis`, read
    from a sealed manifest's `sources[]` (snapshots and the `[lineage]` recorded at sealing) and `raw/origins.jsonl`
    only. Nodes are registry source ids (`<source>/<part>` for a declared part) and upstream artefacts
    (`repo@commit`; `zenodo:<doi>/<file>`, `hf:<dataset>@<revision>`, `<corpus>@<version>`):
    `snapshot_of` (`n` the snapshot's candidates, basis `corpus.json`); the declared `built_on`, `vendored`,
    `cited_by`, `owns`, `excludes` (`n` null); each declared duplicate with its relation (`n` the raw objects whose
    origin path its `path` glob matches, basis `profile [lineage]; raw/origins.jsonl`); and a within-corpus
    `byte_identical` edge (`n` the objects held under more than one origin) when there are any. Sorted by
    `(from_node, relation, to_node)`.
  - **Unavailable.** A corpus whose manifest records no `sources[].lineage` (a working corpus) raises
    `ApiUnavailable`. This closes the `rows(corpus, "lineage")` deviation that D-48 listed in the `agentprov.api`
    docstring.
  - **Tests.** `tests/cli/test_api_lineage_rows.py` on the sealed fixture `mini-mit` (three duplicates entries, a git
    snapshot), plus a variant with the lineage removed; `test_unavailable_parts_say_so` keeps its working corpus.
  - **Rejected:** reading the profile files at query time (the corpus must be self-describing at its sealed
    versions); counting collection manifests or per-execution lineage documents (deferred, AD-10 rows 5-6).
  - **Downstream:** new API behaviour, no corpus bytes.
- **D-542 (2026-10-15, core review C finding CC-18; user decision 2026-10-15: approved, delegated to the orchestrator

    invocation only, while `attempts_per_cell` counted the whole ledger. After a resume the per-model counts covered
    1 of 2 ledgered sessions, and a no-op resume wrote `models: {}`.
  - **Change.** The report rebuilds a `SessionQuality` for every ledger entry from its stored capture log
    (`capture_sha256`, read through the raw store with `session_quality`, as `_ingest` reads a new session), so it
    is a pure function of the corpus (N.2.1b item 12; D.10.9). A quarantined entry stored nothing and is not
    counted; an entry without a capture log counts with no facts, as before. Only `cli/live/campaign.py` changes;
    `cli/run.py` writes the report as before. Test: `tests/integration/test_live_quality_resume.py` (`--repeats 1`,
    then `--repeats 2`, then a no-op resume, with the fake worker environment).
  - **Rejected:** merging counters with the previous `live.quality` (not reproducible from the corpus).
  - **Downstream:** `live.quality` bytes of a resumed live working manifest. Only `test_only` live corpora exist
    and none is regenerated, so no regen item. No sealed corpus bytes.
- **D-543 (2026-10-15, core review C finding CC-28 remainder; user decision 2026-10-15: option (b) approved, delegated
  to the orchestrator and confirmed directly by the user). The consent text names the instrumentation the session will

  - **Problem.** N.1.11(3) required the consent text, printed before the first model call, to list every declared

  - **Change (option b).** N.1.11(3) now says the consent text names the instrumentation the session will declare,

    code change.
  - **Deferred (option a), revisit item.** A protocol op, or an extended `hello_ok`/`plan`, that returns the declared
    instrumentation items so the consent text can list them. It needs a capture/backend protocol change in
    `backends/shared`; revisit in the live-capture phase (G3, the Mac Studio capture machine).

- **D-529 (2026-10-14, `import --sample` for dev test runs; designed by the CLI robustness session on the GUI build's
  request D-544, relayed by the orchestrator; user decisions 2026-10-14: approved; 2026-10-15: containers and
  multi-execution files are expanded or listed in full and only N mapped; it lands early and alone, for the corpus
  pre-check and the GUI dev runs).**
  - **Synopsis:** `agentprov import ... --sample N --sample-mode first|spread|random [--seed S]`. The mode defaults to
    `first`; `--seed` is required for `random` and only there; the option is exclusive with `--limit` and refused with
    `--release`, because a sample is a partial corpus and never released.
  - **Selection happens in the runner** (`adapters/runner/importer.py`, `_plan_sample`), once, before the batch loop,
    from the full list of the import's executions. Membership therefore never depends on `--batch-size`, `--jobs` or
    the resume order (cf. CD-7), and a resume selects the same set.
    - **Whole files:** sample key = the label; only the chosen files are read and stored.
    - **Containers:** every container is stored and expanded, and a `plan_only` container job lists the reader's
      planned units; sample key = `label!/member`. Pass 2 maps each container with every member as input (the plan
      needs them) and a `units` list, so only the chosen units are mapped.
    - **Multi-execution files:** each file is stored and mapped once to list its items (`summarise_unit_frames` heads);
      sample key = `label#<source key>`. Pass 2 re-maps only the files holding a chosen item and seals only those
      items. A file with no item (aborted, not of the dialect) is one unit, kept whole if chosen.
    - Pass 1 keeps its stored files and expansions for pass 2, so nothing is stored twice.
  - **Modes** (`select_sample`): `first`, the first N keys in sorted order; `random`, the N smallest
    `sha256(utf8(S) || 0x00 || utf8(key))` (no PRNG state); `spread`, strata in sorted order taken round-robin, each
    in key order. The stratum comes from a reader hook `sample_stratum(key) -> str | None`. Each hook lands
    as its own family-only branch after this one, as invariant 5 and the new-family guards require: `inspect.eval`
    (the `.eval` log), `autogen.runs` (`phase<N>[/<arm>]`) and `credleak.cell` (`<section>/<channel>`), each from its
    own documented path grammar. A reader without the hook refuses `spread` (exit 5,
    `import.sample.unsupported`); nothing is guessed from paths.
  - **Recording:** the working manifest gets `partial: true` and `selection.sample = {n, mode, seed, candidates,
    selected, stratum}`, written only when used; the summary counts `sampled_out`; `package` refuses a partial corpus. A
    recompute that re-maps a sampled corpus replays its recorded sample, so NEW holds the same executions. Ordinary
    imports are byte-identical (no new manifest key or counter, no new job param).
  - **Byte class 1** (regen-batch item 102): `adapters/runner/` moves the `aer` stage's `engine_code_sha256`, and each
    hook branch moves its family's `adapter_code_sha256`. A sampled unit maps to exactly the AER, SEM and PROV bytes
    it has in a full import.
  - **Rejected:**
    - CLI-side selection of input files (it samples files, not executions, and cannot see members, items or arms);
    - a PRNG such as `random.Random(seed).sample` (its algorithm is not a stable contract, and the result would depend
      on order);
    - stratifying by path components the reader does not define (a guess);
    - sampling container members by raw member rows (a log's header member is not an execution and is needed to plan).
    - Build sequenced by the orchestrator: after D-414, D-460 and `claude/derive-bugpass`, on a held branch, with regen items from `reserve_id`.
  - **Pre-round review addendum (2026-10-22; report `docs/reports/pre-round-review/report.md`, re-check RC-4; regen
    items 153 and 154; commits `f3e39ec9`, `5ed5e3f8`).** Two pass-1 behaviours change for multi-execution readers:
    - **PR-9, sampled-out files are no longer collapsed.** Pass 1 used to apply the D-202 collapse (or the resume count)
      to a file that another snapshot (or an earlier run) holds sealed whole as soon as it was stored, before the draw:
      a sampled-out file was then listed under the sampled snapshot, with a `dedup.collapsed` entry. Pass 1 now only
      lists such a file under its `<id>#` key (`<id>` is the candidate's sample identity, its label or, for a D-530
      pinned object, `label\x00pinned`). The collapse or resume is applied after the draw, and only when that key was
      drawn. A full import still collapses as before (D-202).
    - **PR-11 #3, a file whose rows are refused is one unit in pass 1.** A file whose rejected rows fail validation
      (D-321) is sealed whole in pass 2. Pass 1 now lists it under its `<id>#` key too, instead of its items. Before,
      the first run drew over the item keys and a resume over the `<id>#` key (NF-34), so a `random` or `spread` resume
      could draw another set.
    - Byte class 1 through `importer.py` (the `aer` engine digest). A sampled corpus is never released, so no kept corpus
      changes.
- **D-520..D-524 (2026-10-14, CLI robustness Part A, branch `cli-robustness`; the six gaps of the GUI research were
  directed by the user through the orchestrator session; the design choices below are this session's, for the user's
  review).** All are byte class 0: `cli/`, `io/`, `raw/fetch.py`, `migration/gates.py`, `corpus/package.py` and
  `render/` are in no stage code digest, and no AER, SEM or PROV byte changes.
- **D-520 (signals).** SIGHUP joins SIGINT and SIGTERM: the first one raises `Interrupted` (a `KeyboardInterrupt`), so
  the command flushes, seals what it can, releases its lock and exits 130. A SIGHUP inherited as ignored (`nohup`) stays
  ignored. The summary notice names the signal. The second signal kills the live T2 worker trees before `os._exit(130)`
  (CC-27).
  - **Rejected:**
    - exit 129 for SIGHUP (one interrupted code is what N.1.3 and resume tooling expect);
    - ignoring SIGHUP outright (a closed terminal should still stop the job, cleanly).
- **D-521 (shared state outside a corpus: guard G6a).** Two primitives in `agentprov.io.locks` reuse G6's `O_EXCL`
  record `{pid, host, command, started}`:
  - `ResourceLock`, exclusive. It covers the fetch cache's write path (`<cache>/.agentprov.lock`; cached reads never
    lock) and a backend environment's build (`$AGENTPROV_HOME/locks/envs/<env>.lock`).
  - `ResourceUse`, shared registrations. `run` registers as a user of its environment and of staging; a build refuses
    while a live user exists, and a run refuses during a build.

  **Bounded:** no lock waits, and a dead holder on this host is removed, because every protected operation is
  idempotent. A live, foreign or unreadable holder refuses at once with `io.resource_busy` (exit 4), naming the holder.
  - **Rejected:**
    - `fcntl`/`msvcrt` locks (a platform branch, D-7);
    - waiting for the lock (a hung holder would hang every job; the GUI serialises with slots, D-392);
    - `--break-stale-lock` for these (unlike a corpus, nothing here needs a human to judge a resume);
    - one lock per cache entry (`acquisitions.jsonl` and `purge --cache` span the cache; writes are rare);
    - lock files inside `envs/` or staging (`info` lists `envs/`, and staging directories are scanned as evidence).
- **D-522 (`migrate` output location).** Gate reports default to `$AGENTPROV_HOME/migration/reports` and gate E's
  semantic diff to `$AGENTPROV_HOME/migration/semdiff`. A report meant to be committed is written to the checkout on
  purpose (`--reports-dir`/`--semdiff-dir`). The gate-order check also reads the checkout's `migration/reports`, so
  committed reports keep counting. J.3.0/J.3.6 ("committed") need a matching edit by the J owner.
  - **Rejected:**
    - keeping the repository default (a job manager's run dirties the checkout);
    - dropping the repository lookup (committed release reports would stop satisfying J.3.0).
- **D-523 (`--progress-file` floor; `agentprov-progress/0.1` unchanged).** The file shows the `--progress` level but
  never below `status`, and it is written at `off`.
  - Commands without stderr feedback still write `start` and `end`.
  - Corpus-level stages are reported as units of a known total: `package` seal stages, `verify` levels and
    `backends build` stages. A `status`-level reader therefore sees them.
  - `fetch` reports one unit per recipe.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a new `stage` event kind now (that is 0.2, D-393);
    - a `steps` floor (one line per stage per unit, about 230k lines for a 38k import).
- **D-524 (`render` layout limit).** An image is laid out only for a graph of at most `--max-edges` edges (default 800;
  0 = no limit). Above it the `.dot` text is written, `dot` is not started, and the execution fails with
  `render.graph_too_large`, with one message naming the remedies.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a per-bundle mode (the assessment bundle alone reaches 2,342 nodes, so it does not help the large case);
    - `dot` fast flags by default (they change the drawing of every render);
    - a higher timeout (minutes per execution under `--jobs 4`).
- **D-525 (2026-10-14, CLI robustness Part B: how the GUI core prerequisites land; user answers 2026-10-14).**
  - **D-395's core part** is `run --env-stdin` only. `keyring` stays in `gui/`; the CLI never reads a keychain (D-447).
  - **Built now (byte class 0), on `cli-robustness`:** everything outside `adapters/runner/`. That is D-397's `json`
    format, D-395, progress 0.2 in the CLI sink (D-526), the control file (D-527), and G2c-5's reader with the seal and
    verify refusals.
  - **Deferred** to the regen-batch entry "cli-robustness GUI-prerequisite pipeline", built when the files are free
    and landed before the regeneration round:
    - D-393: the import `stage`/`unit_kind` events, the T1 pool reporter and the per-level verify events;
    - D-394: the true drain of `import`, `derive`, `recompute` and `run`;
    - G2c-5: the producers and the `validate --corpus` clearing.
  - **Until then,** a drain degrades to a stop, saying so in the `control` acknowledgement.
  - **G2c-5's mark** follows design §8.3a: `validation.prov_conformance: "skipped"` in the working `corpus.json`,
    written only when the skip was used.
  - **Rejected:**
    - editing `importer.py` now (owned by `pipeline-perf`, and in the `aer` stage digest);
    - refusing drain outright (the GUI's "Pause" would do nothing).
  - **Pre-round review addendum (2026-10-22; report `docs/reports/pre-round-review/report.md`, re-check RC-4 and RC-9;
    regen item 152 for PR-7, item 150 for PR-6; commit `f3e39ec9`).**
    - **PR-6, the drain.** `import` honours a drain; the re-map inside `recompute`, `derive` and `verify --level
      rederive` does not (`import_source(..., drain=True)` from `import` only), so a drain sent to those degrades to a
      stop (MN N.1.10(5)). Before, it truncated NEW, which was then reported as failures.
    - **PR-7, `--skip-prov-conformance` and resume.** The setting is now part of a recompute's resume identity: the
      validation stage definition in `derived_from` carries its `skipped` checks, so a recompute interrupted under one
      setting and resumed under the other is refused (exit 4, `corpus.derive.resume_mismatch`; MN N.1.8(3)). Before,
      the resumed NEW claimed full tier 4 while some rows held no PV checks. The reuse key (D-30) carries the setting
      too.
    - **RC-9, reuse.** Reuse is one key per execution over its SEM, PROV and validation together. So a recompute whose
      setting differs from its source's validation (a skip recompute of a fully validated source, or the reverse)
      reuses no execution and recomputes SEM and PROV too. That is correct and slower than needed. Carrying the source's
      SEM and PROV while recomputing only the validation would need reuse split per stage; that is deferred to after
      the round. A recompute under the setting its source was validated with reuses as before. **Superseded
      2026-10-22 (D-623 scope extension):** a skip recompute of a fully validated source now carries SEM and PROV and
      rebuilds only the validation rows.
    - Byte class: PR-7 is class 0 (`corpus/derive.py` is in no stage digest); PR-6 is class 1 (`importer.py`).
- **D-526 (2026-10-14, progress 0.2 as built; refines D-393).**
  - **`seq`** is assigned when an event is queued, up to the file's level, so a gap is a drop. The `run` line is
    reserved `seq` 0.
  - **Run id:** a UUIDv7 per process.
  - **The `run` header** holds pid, command, mode, dry run, jobs, the corpus root and the summary path (escaped and
    home-redacted), the software version and `segment`.
  - **`heartbeat`** is an absolute snapshot from the producer-side counters. It is written every `--progress-interval`
    (default 2 s, 1..3600), at each `stage` end and before `end`.
  - **Rotation** past `--progress-max-bytes` (default 8 MiB, at least 64 KiB) renames the file to `PATH.1` and starts
    the new file with a `run` line and a heartbeat.
  - **Stages:** `package`, `verify` and `backends build` emit `stage` events and keep their unit events.
  - **Rejected:**
    - assigning `seq` at write time (drops would be invisible);
    - heartbeats on stderr's plain or tty renderers (display noise; those renderers keep their own status line);
    - more than one rotated file (design §5.3 bounds disk use to two segments).
- **D-527 (2026-10-14, the control file as built; refines D-394).**
  - **Polling:** a daemon thread `stat`s the file at most once a second. It is not polled per unit, because the
    commands' unit loops are in other sessions' files; one `stat` per second meets the "≤ once per second inside long
    units" bound.
  - **Ignored:** a request already present at start, and a seen nonce.
  - **`stop`** is `_thread.interrupt_main(SIGTERM)`, the first-SIGTERM path, which is graceful on Windows too.
  - **The summary notice** names the request and nonce.
  - **Rejected:**
    - acting on a request present at start (re-running the same argv after a drain would stop at once);
    - `os.kill` of the own pid (not graceful on Windows).
- **D-528 (2026-10-14, `run --env-stdin` details; refines D-395).**
  - **Accepted names:** the union of `api_key_env`, `base_url_env` and `model_env` over `endpoints.toml`, plus
    `REASONING_EFFORT`. The selected endpoint's names are then taken, as from `.env`.
  - **Values are strings.** A `*_API_KEY` value, or the value of an unknown name, is registered for redaction before
    any message is formed.
  - **Refused with `--llm-script`** (a scripted run needs no key) and exclusive with `--env-file`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - accepting only the selected endpoint's names (the GUI sends one object per endpoint choice, so this is the same
      thing; the union keeps the parser independent of model selection);
    - reading stdin after model selection (D-395 says before any other step).
- **D-570 (2026-10-15, phase 10o part C: a sibling family `qwencode`; user-approved 2026-10-15).** The Qwen Code runs of
  RedCode-Exec (Zenodo 23168099, `trajectories_Qwen-qwen3coder.zip`, 3,300 runs) are `qwen --output-format json` stdout:
  one JSON array of Claude-Code-SDK-shaped messages (`system`/`init`, `assistant` with provider content blocks, `user` with
  `tool_result` blocks, `result`), Qwen Code 0.21.0. They are read by a new family `qwencode` (dialect `qwencode.json`,
  variant `v0.21`).
  - **Rejected:** a variant of `geminicli` (array versus JSONL, nested provider messages versus flat events, provider
    tool ids versus CLI ids, no timestamps; a second reader and mapper under a misleading family name).
- **D-571 (2026-10-15, part C: identity and corpus; user-approved).** Source and profile `redcode-exec-qwencode`, part
  `qwen3coder`, pins `runs` (the Qwen zip) and `supp` (the supplementary zip, a context pin). Corpus `redcode-exec`,
  shared with `redcode-exec-openhands` (one corpus per source, D-144); see the amendment below. Task header as for the OpenHands part: benchmark
  `redcode-exec`, suite = language, `task_id` = `<scenario>_<payload>`, `attack_id` = the target's request type.
  - **Amended 2026-10-15 (user decision, relayed by the orchestrator): separate corpora per agent;** corpus
    `redcode-exec-qwencode` beside `redcode-exec-openhands` (the OpenHands part's existing corpus id). Cross-agent
    comparison is an analysis step, not a corpus. The shared `redcode-exec` corpus above is withdrawn.
- **D-572 (2026-10-15, part C: the AER mapping; user-approved).** `init` → header `ext` and the harness actor (version
  0.21.0, O). A block (consecutive assistant events between tool results) → one class-I `model_call`, checked against
  `result.num_turns` (equal in 3,295/3,295). Each assistant event's blocks → the block's assistant message: `text` parts
  and `tool_call` parts with `provider_call_id` = `id` and `args` = `input` (O). Each `tool_result` → a `tool_execution`
  (status `error` iff `is_error`) and a tool message answering the call by `tool_use_id`. Sub-agent `system` events →
  harness activities; other user `text` events → user messages (`unattributed_additional_user_message`). `result` → run
  status `ok` (D) and `ext`, with profile checks (final text, turns, usage). No time anywhere; `duration_ms` in `ext`.
- **D-573 (2026-10-15, part C: prompt, rules and API samples; user-approved).** The joined RedCode prompt (dataset for S1,
  prompt-generator output for S2/S3, after the harness's `/sys/kernel` rewrite) is a `task_prompt` fixture: content O, class
  I (the run never shows what was sent on stdin). `execution_rules.md` (copied to `/app/QWEN.md`) is an `other` fixture (I).
  The group's `_full_api_request_sample.json` is a supporting artefact with no fixture and no relation (captured with a
  dummy prompt and the settings moved aside). Every run raises `qwencode.user_message_not_logged`.
- **D-574 (2026-10-15, part C: code verification; user-approved).** Every reading of Qwen Code behaviour is class I
  (`_unverified`); fetching the Qwen Code 0.21.0 sources to raise them to D needs the user's own yes. The deposit's
  harness code (`Qwen_evaluation/`) is documentary evidence (agentops D-193 policy).
- **D-575 (2026-10-15, part C: model identity; user-approved).** `model.requested` = `init.model` (O); `model.served`
  `not_recorded`; `message.model` in `ext`.
- **D-576 (2026-10-15, part C: outcomes; user-approved).** Each run's score record (`conversation_log/index<sc>.json`)
  gives the judgement `score` (actor `redcode_qwen_scorer`, origin checker I; 1 is `ambiguous`); `step_count`,
  `exceeded_soft_iteration_cap`, `used_write_tool`, `timed_out` and `last_response_full` stay in `ext`. SEM reads 3 as
  executed, 0 as not, 1 as not informative.
- **D-577 (2026-10-15, part C: the non-runs; option (b) user-approved).** The 4 runs cut at exactly 65,536 B are mapped
  from the complete top-level events before the cut, with `qwencode.truncated_capture` and `incomplete_run`. Implementation
  (stated at build time): `agentprov.ingest.jsonstream` is fail-closed and yields nothing for a truncated document, so the
  reader tries, from the end, each `}` that may close a top-level element and parses `prefix + "]"` with
  `strict_json_loads`; the first that parses is the salvaged prefix (bounded number of tries; the stored bytes are never
  edited; the cut offset and the number of events kept are recorded). A salvaged file is not valid JSON as a whole, so
  its messages are cited by byte-range locators (`{"a", "bytes": [start, end], "p"}`, C.9.1), each span checked to parse
  strictly to its message; an array pointer would dangle (found by the scratch trial's evidence-linkage tier, 2026-10-15). The empty output is registered
  `select.not_execution_artefact` (`qwencode.empty_output`); the 5 API samples are supporting artefacts, not executions.
- **D-578 (2026-10-15, part C: secrets; user-approved).** No `[withhold]` table (no credential-shaped value); payload
  e-mails and keys kept as published (D-179 option A); fixtures byte-identical, none holding a home path.
  - **Amendment (2026-10-21; the bug pass's D-602, user-approved that day; orchestrator routing).** The deposit's
    supplementary zip (the `supp` pin, shared with `redcode-exec-openhands`) holds a real-format Hugging Face access
    token in an unselected member, `environment/<seg>/.bash_history`. Its validity was never tested, and the value is
    not recorded. `redcode-exec-qwencode` version 2 gains D-602's rule: `hf-token-shape`, pattern `hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{34}`,
    `scope = "object"`, with `scan_rules = ["huggingface-access-token"]`. The decoded scan withholds the zip container,
    and no execution, once the zip is stored. Until archive context (D-530) and corpus/0.2 (NF-24) let a qwencode corpus

- **D-592 (2026-10-21, seagent: the dropped calls of a blocked batch; user-approved 2026-10-21; built on held branch
  `artefact-seagent-pc01`, stacked on `regen-held-3`; integration order held-3, artefact-catalogues, this branch).** The guard drops the other calls of a blocked batch (166 calls in 107 logs). Version 1
  maps them by position:

    generic `agentdojo.unexecuted_trailing_calls` count, however, read 558 calls in 424 logs against the declared 392 in

    digest, which item 136 already moves); the fixture pins are unchanged.

- **D-601 (2026-10-21, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, pre-check PC-01, PC-02 (with PC-07); user decision 2026-10-21:
  approved, redaction of both pointer classes plus object-scope withholding of the token-bearing raw objects).**
  WhistleBench (D.9.7) leaked two things into its AERs. (1) In 28 `awareness_blackbox` logs the header's
  `eval.revision.origin` is a clone URL whose userinfo holds a GitHub-token-shaped value. The mapper copies it to the
  bench actor's `ext.inspect.revision.origin` and to `code.repo` (`mapper.py`, the bench actor). D-182's harness
  pointers covered the first and not the second. (2) In 260 samples the `error_retries` tracebacks (`traceback`,
  `traceback_ansi`) name one workstation home directory (account #1). The mapper copies them to the run scope's
  `ext.inspect.error_retries`, which no harness pointer covered.
  - **Decision:**
    - **`redact.py`.** `HARNESS_POINTERS` gains `/code/repo` (actor) and `/ext/inspect/error_retries` (scope). A
      `harness_text` rule may declare `pointers`: a non-empty list of distinct record-relative pointers, each a harness
      class or below one; the rule then applies only there (`family.schema.json` too). Inspect has no `ext.lex` key
      pointer that can hold either span: its lexical hints are float positions, and the keys under `revision` and
      `error_retries` are fixed, so nothing beyond BF-21's model-id handling is needed.
    - **Profile `whistlebench@2`.** `origin_userinfo` (pattern `(?<=://)[^/@\s"]{1,256}(?=@)`, `pointers` the two
      revision copies) replaces the userinfo with the literal `redacted`: no digest of a credential is recorded. The
      collision check of D.9.12 stays as it is, so a literal label admits one span per unit. A unit with two distinct
      userinfos fails closed (ProfileError, the unit is not mapped) and is never collapsed silently. The census has at
      most one per log. `retry_account` (pattern `(?<=/Users/)[^/\s"'<>\\]{1,64}(?=/)`, `pointers =
      ["/ext/inspect/error_retries"]`) gives the account segment `<account:{span12}>` (D-182). The label holds `<` and
      `>`, which the pattern excludes, so it is never matched again. Quirk `inspect.error_retries`. Each redacted pointer
      is tagged D and cites `inspect.value_redacted@1`, with one info issue `inspect.value_redacted` per unit (D.9.12).
    - **`[withhold]`.** Reason `secret`, `scan_rules = ["github-pat"]`, one pattern rule `github-token-shape`
      (`gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,255}`), scope `object`. The AER holds the redacted copy only, so no derived-file hit
      escalates (D-235). A release seal withholds each token-bearing `header.json` (basis `profile_rule`) with its
      `.eval` container (basis `container`). The decoded scan (D-450) reaches the same 28 containers through the
      unselected `_journal/start.json` and leaves the `container` basis (shown end to end). No execution is withheld.
    - **D-31.** Version 2. Version 1 ships as `profiles/archive/whistlebench.profile.v1.toml` with main's bytes
      (sha256 `2275688dea24…`), the digest that the pre-check scratch partials `l2-final-runs-j1`/`j2` record. The two
      phase-10f scratch partials (`whistlebench-j8`, `whistlebench-j3-s5`) record `whistlebench@1` at `71d7fc2f3103…`,
      the bytes before regeneration-batch item 16. Item 16 changed the profile without a bump, before D-31's strict
      rule. Those partials cannot be rebuilt at either archived version and are scratch only (not archived; the F-8
      ruling is to rebuild at their building commit). Pinned in `tests/unit/test_d31_bumps.py`. The registry part names
      no version.
  - **Census** (the pinned bare clone `legobridge/whistlebench@9c27637c`, `final_runs/`: 223 blobs, 523,183,391 bytes;
    counts only):
    - Withhold pattern over the raw blobs as stored: 2 hits. Both are context `logs.json` files
      (`awareness_blackbox/habench_summarization`, `awareness_blackbox/snitchbench`), which the Inspect import does not
      store (its mapper consumes no context), and 0 of the 184 `.eval` containers (compressed).
    - Decoded members: `header.json` 28 of 184, `_journal/start.json` 28 of 184, **0 of 9,200 sample members** (the
      primary objects of the executions), and 0 in every other member class. All 28 logs are in `awareness_blackbox`.
    - URL userinfo: 28 logs with 1 distinct span each, 156 with none. The matches sit in `header.json` and
      `_journal/start.json` only.
    - Account #1: 260 samples, 722 `error_retries` strings, nowhere else in the tree. Other `/Users/<x>/` segments (9
      distinct) are the benchmark's scenarios: inputs, messages, scores, store, attachments, output, events, and 129
      logger events (`_call_tools.py` tool-argument lines, `scorers.py` warnings). They are content or quote model
      tool arguments, which is why `retry_account` is narrowed (D-604).
    - Pre-check partial `l2-final-runs-j1` (154 logs, stored at version 1): 28 raw `header.json` objects and 1,400
      AER files hold the token shape; 0 PROV files.
    - Scratch re-map at version 2 (every pinned log, in process, nothing kept): 184 logs, 9,200 executions, 0
      register entries, 0 degenerate, 0 failures. `origin_userinfo` redacted 2,800 strings in 1,400 executions (1,400 at
      `/code/repo`, 1,400 at `/ext/inspect/revision/origin`), and `retry_account` 722 strings in 260 executions (all at
      `/ext/inspect/error_retries`). Residue in the AER bytes: 0 executions hold the token shape and 0 hold account #1.
      The 1,400 userinfo forms left are the literal.
  - **Byte impact:** class 1, whistlebench only. AER: the bench actor (`code.repo`, `ext.inspect.revision.origin`,
    `evf`, `rule`, `ext.inspect.redacted`) of the 1,400 executions of the 28 logs, and the run scope of the 260
    executions with an account path. The header's profile ref moves to `whistlebench@2` and its digest changes in every
    execution's AER (9,200) and everything that cites it. PROV and validation follow the AER. The `inspect` adapter code
    digest moves (`redact.py`). No other profile declares redaction rules, so no other corpus and no golden pin moves.
    No corpus is stored (scratch partials only). Regeneration-batch item 144.
  - **Settled after the build (user decisions 2026-10-21):** the release seal needed a semantics profile (H.3.1); see
    the addendum below. The 260 raw sample members that hold account #1 ship as pinned (D-186 (c)): no exact withhold
    rule targets them, and D-604's object-scope rule is not extended to them. The datasheet discloses them.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a `{span12}` label for the userinfo (a digest of a credential);
    - letting a literal label collapse distinct spans (silent; the collision check fails closed instead);
    - an unnarrowed traceback rule (it would rewrite scenario home directories quoted from model tool arguments in
      logger events);
    - `executions` scope (no sample member and no redacted AER holds the value; it would drop 1,400 runs for a header
      field);
    - editing version 1 in place (scratch partials record it, D-31).
  - Tests: `tests/adapters/inspect/test_d601_whistlebench_redact.py` (pointers, literal and salted labels, fail-closed
    collision, narrowing, the shipped profile's mapping, version 1 leaving the value, the rule). Also
    `tests/adapters/inspect/test_whistlebench_withhold_e2e.py` (release import, seal, `chain --release`, deposit,
    sidecar).
  - **Addendum (2026-10-21, user decisions 2026-10-21: a dedicated semantics profile, so that a release seal works;
    the raw traceback samples ship as pinned with a datasheet disclosure).**

      `adapters/inspect/semantics/inspect.whistlebench-1/tables.toml` and `semantics/whistlebench.py`; the family's

    - Tests: `tests/adapters/inspect/test_whistlebench_semantics.py`, and the end-to-end test now seals with it and

  - **Addendum 2 (2026-10-21, user decision 2026-10-21: a WhistleBench semantics profile v2 from the scorer and task
    code).**

      scope `tool_output`: the text of every part of a tool message (a `$utf16` text is decoded, rewritten and
      re-encoded). The pattern applies inside the text, so an account-segment pattern keeps the path
      (`/home/acct-<12 hex>/…`). A mapper post-pass (as Inspect's `_redact`) tags each rewritten pointer `D`, cites
      `openhands.value_redacted@1`, lists `{p, rule}` in `ext.openhands.redacted` and adds one info issue

      `ACCOUNT_ALLOWLIST`; replacement `acct-{span12}`. Refined from the investigation's pattern: the root boundary was

- **D-607 (2026-10-21, bug pass bugpass-perf-10, pre-check PC-dtap-bench-01; user decision 2026-10-21: approved, labels
  allowlist).**
  - **Context:** the DTap pre-check (`docs/reports/precheck/dtap-bench.md`, PC-01, S0) found five named workstation
    accounts of the harness hosts in 1,094 trajectory files: tool output, OpenClaw harness-config state
    (`/trajectory/*/state/plugins|agents|storePath`), agent arguments, agent text and final responses. Accounts #1, #3,
    #4 and #5 reach the L2 scratch AER and PROV. Account #2 (301 files, the harness-config account) reaches them on a
    full import. 137 other named account strings (1,393 in 301 files, 133 distinct names) are benchmark or model
    content. No DTap profile declared a redaction rule, so the AER, SEM and PROV of a full import would carry the five
    names. The user chose (2026-10-21) the option "exact, 0 collateral, over every AER string". It is an exception to
    D-604 (redact in tool and environment output only; model-authored text verbatim) for this source.
  - **Decision:**
    - A closed profile table `[[family.dtap.redact]]` `{id, scope, pattern, replacement, labels, note?}` and the module
      `adapters/dtap/redact.py`, a family copy of D-476's grammar. The only scope is `all_strings`: every string of
      every record the mapper writes, model-authored text included. The pass runs after the records are built, so it
      also covers ext copies and `ext.lex` member orders.
    - A pattern is structural, names no account and has a named group `span`. The replacement is
      `acct-{span12}`, with D-476's `{span12}` (first 12 hex of SHA-256 over `<profile id> NUL <span>`). It replaces
      the span only, so `/home/<n>/.ssh` becomes `/home/acct-<label>/.ssh`.
    - Only a match whose label the rule's `labels` list holds is redacted. Every other account is left as it is.
      `dtap-bench@2` lists six labels: the five PC-01 accounts and the one other letter case in which the data spells
      account #3 (109 occurrences). They were computed out of band (`python3 -I`, in memory) from the names in the
      pinned data. The five accounts were identified by the pre-check's own classification (the verifier's
      `v_acc.json` targets, which equal the four L2-reaching non-task-tree digests of `acc_l2.json` and the 301-file
      harness-config digest of `raw.json`). The repository holds only labels an AER would carry anyway, never a name.
    - Three rules share the list (the two token rules and the case-variant label: user decision 2026-10-21: kept
      (label-gated, 0 collateral)):
      - `host_account`: the account segment of an account path, in the forms and endings of the release scan's D-457
        rule, over decoded strings (`/home/<n>`, `/Users/<n>`, `\/home\/<n>`, `/mnt/<d>/Users/<n>`,
        `C:\Users\<n>`, `C:\\Users\\<n>`, `C:/Users/<n>`; trailing dots kept outside the span);
      - `host_account_token`: a whole letter-and-digit token, in any context;
      - `host_account_dotted`: a token whose letter runs are joined by single `.`, `_` or `-` (one listed name has
        such a separator).
    - The census showed that the path rule alone leaves the listed names in `ls -l` owner and group columns, munged
      project-directory names (`-Users-<n>-…`), deeper roots (`/home/<generic>/<n>/`), paths right after an escaped
      newline (`\n/home/<n>`) and plain text. The two token rules close that residue and stay exact, because a token is
      redacted only when its label is listed.
    - Pointers (`evf` and `unk` keys, scoped rule citations, `ext.lex.ord` keys and `ext.lex.flt`) are redacted token
      by token. A renamed object key and the pointers that name it stay in step, and two pointer tokens never join
      into a path. A recorded member order (`ext.lex.ord`) stays a permutation: `redacted` is appended when it is added
      to `ext.dtap`.
    - Source locators (`src`) keep pointing at the raw field. Raw bytes are untouched and ship as pinned
      (D-186 (c)).
    - Recording: each redacted pointer is tagged `D` (an `I` stays `I`) and cites the new rule
      `dtap.value_redacted@1` (D). `ext.dtap.redacted` lists `{p, rule: "dtap-bench@2#<rule id>"}`. One info seal issue
      `dtap.value_redacted` carries the count. Artefact entry `dtap.art.host_account_paths` (FO).
    - Two spans with one listed label are a `ProfileError`, as in D-476.
  - **Census (2026-10-21, the pinned runs snapshot `836caf2f` in staging, mapped in process with the shipped mapper and
    `dtap-bench@2`; counts only):**
