- **D-690..D-699 (2026-10-22, local LLM endpoints; design note `docs/reports/local-llm/design.md`; user decisions
  2026-10-22: Q1-Q7 and the LAN design, "yes to all").** Live runs can use models served on this machine (and, opted
  in, on a private LAN), and the user sees and picks the exact model in the CLI and the GUI (the GUI calls the CLI).
  - **D-690, servers.** `endpoints.toml` gains `lmstudio` (`127.0.0.1:1234`), `mlx_lm` (`:8080`, concurrency 1),
    `llamacpp` (`:8080`) and `vllm` (`:8000`) beside `ollama` and `omlx`, each `local = true`, keyless, with its own
    `base_url_env` (`OMLX_BASE_URL` added to `omlx`). A required key `server` names the kind on every local entry
    (`endpoint.registry.server`), and a local entry speaks `openai_chat` only (`endpoint.registry.local_api`; with
    D-656's `api`). Concurrency is set only where the server's default is fixed; LM Studio and llama.cpp report theirs.
    Tool-call behaviour per server is in the file's comments; the preflight decides (A4). **Rejected:** a per-entry
    tool-call flag (the behaviour depends on the model and the server's flags, not the server alone).
  - **D-691, discovery.** A new application command `agentprov models` (MN N.2.17 table, section N.2.18; N.2 keeps its fifteen), loopback-only and read-only: it
    fingerprints the server (Ollama `/api/version`+`/api/tags`, LM Studio `/api/v1/models`, llama.cpp `/props`, vLLM
    `/version`; oMLX and mlx_lm record `openai_generic`), refuses the wrong kind on a shared default port (exit 4), and
    lists the served models; `--format json` is the GUI picker's source. `run` wires the N.2.1a(1) preflight: a
    missing or unlisted `--model-id` exits 3 naming the served ids (a numbered pick on a terminal). `run --base-url`
    (precedence `--base-url` > `.env` > settings > registry). `http.client` only, the connected peer checked, no
    proxy, no redirect, strict bounded JSON through `agentprov.ingest`. **Rejected:** `run SOURCE --list-models`
    (listing does not depend on a source); `urllib` (honours `HTTP_PROXY`).
  - **D-692, identity record.** `agentprov-local-model/0.1`: observed facts only, each citing a response digest or
    a file digest; `identity_sha256` is the JCS digest of the server identity and the files. Files come from the HF
    cache (64-hex LFS blob names give weight digests, recorded as `hf_blob_name`), LM Studio's `downloadsFolder`
    (tied to the served key by name prefix **and** the exact `size_bytes` the server reports, since the key is not the
    directory name on LM Studio 0.4.23), or `--model-dir`. Weights are hashed by default (Q3) with a digest cache in
    `$AGENTPROV_HOME/cache/model-digests.jsonl` (a dry run never writes it); `--no-hash-weights` records sizes only.
    No absolute path is recorded. **Rejected:** a bare model name as identity (CLAUDE.md research rule).
  - **D-693, recording.** The record (without `observed_at` and nulls) is `agent.local_model`, so it enters
    `plan_sha256` and the config digest: another model is another configuration (G5). T0 re-observes the server side
    before every cell (Q6) and passes it in `run_cell.local_model`; the worker writes the header note
    `agentdojo/local_model` (capture/0.1 unchanged, D-19; not mapped). The manifest's `live` block gains
    `local_models` per config digest. **Rejected:** observation by the worker (T2 cannot read the model files under
    the sandbox, and T0 is the trusted process).
  - **D-694, served model.** A12: a reply whose `served_model` is absent or differs from its request's model is a
    canary condition for every endpoint (Q4), unless the operator accepts that served id with
    `--accept-served-model ID` (recorded as `live.accepted_served_models`). LM Studio models without native tool use
    are refused unless `--allow-text-tool-calls` (Q5: the server adds its own tool prompt, invisible to the capture).
  - **D-695, drift.** A14 (A13 is taken by benchmark validity in D.10.9): a session whose `local_model` note does not match the plan's server-side identity is a
    canary condition. The quality report gains `served_models`, `served_model_mismatch` and `local_model_drift`.
  - **D-696, estimate.** A local endpoint costs $0; the time estimate needs a measured throughput (printed as such)
    until one exists. The GUI's estimator (D-701) reads the registry's `local` flag.
  - **D-697, containment.** With D-664 a loopback endpoint's port is the profile's `LOOPBACK_PORT` (no proxy);
    `localhost` is accepted (the profile covers `::1`, verified by the Inspect session). Stated limit: containment
    covers T0 and T2, not the user's server process; a server that forwards inference off the machine is detected only
    when it says so (Ollama cloud models are listed `remote` and refused, exit 4).
  - **D-698, LAN endpoints (user-approved).** `--allow-lan-endpoint` (run and models), per run, never a stored
    setting: a literal private address only (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, fc00::/7;
    `agentprov_capture.endpoints.is_private_lan_host`), plain http allowed, keyless (an agent with `allow_lan` and a key
    is refused), the address recorded as given (`network: "lan"`; user decision 2026-10-22, confirmed when re-asked:
    the full address, not `lan` plus the port), no local file lookup for a LAN model. Under sandbox-exec the worker reaches it through the D-664 egress
    proxy's HTTP forward mode, for exactly the run's LAN address and port (landed 2026-10-22, D-664 entry below; the
    interim refusal `cli.refused.lan_containment` is removed). **Rejected:** a T0 TCP relay with the base URL rewritten (the recorded request
    would differ from what the client built); host names (can be made to resolve anywhere).
  - **D-699, settings.** A local endpoint's base URL can be stored with `agentprov settings set
    endpoints.<name>.base_url URL` (D-703's store; its validator accepts loopback hosts and literal private addresses
    only). `run` and `models` use it when no `--base-url` (and, for `run`, no `.env` value) is given: precedence
    `--base-url` > `.env` `*_BASE_URL` > the setting > the registry default (`localmodels.configured_base_url`). A
    stored LAN address still needs `--allow-lan-endpoint` on each run (the opt-in is never stored). The formats
    `agentprov-local-models/0.1` and `agentprov-local-model/0.1` join the closed set (`formats.py`).
  - **Class 0** throughout (capture endpoint data, backends/shared, cli/, testing/, tests): no AER, SEM or PROV
    bytes. Commits A (d6b141a2), A2 (43d626a6), B (53262091) and B2 (3b72991a) change the capture and backend
    packages, so every built environment's identity changes (env-rebuild window). **Follow-up offered (class 1):**

- **D-700 (2026-10-22, reverse CLI parity; user requirement relayed by the orchestrator; the forks decided by the user in
  the GUI session's window the same day).**
  - **What.** Everything that can be set or done in the GUI that affects a run, its data, the estimate or stored state
    is also possible through the CLI, with one implementation that the GUI itself calls.
  - **Test.** A GUI registry of settings and actions, each mapped to its CLI command or option, and a test that fails
    on an unmapped entry. Exclusions are allowed only for presentational settings (theme, palette, text size, native
    toolbar, window geometry, viewer limits) and for "which checkout's CLI the GUI runs".
  - **User decisions.**
    - The shared code (prices, estimate, priors, the dev-run planner) moves from `gui/` into the core.
    - `keyring` becomes a core dependency, loaded only in a `python -I` helper process with the D-655 allowlist.
    - The job manager moves into the core (`$AGENTPROV_HOME/jobs`; old GUI jobs are not migrated).
  - **Pieces:** D-701 prices and estimate, D-702 keys, D-703 settings, D-704 jobs and batches, D-705 dev runs.
  - **Spec:** MN N.2.17 lists them as application commands, outside N.2's fifteen.
  - **Class 0:** cli/ and the new modules are outside every stage closure.
  - **The test as built (train 3).**
    - `agentprov_gui/parity.py` is the registry. Settings panes declare `KEYS` (input → `agentprov settings` key);
      Run live inputs are `run` form fields or name their `run` option; buttons and menu actions are a `FORMS` title,
      the command they run, or presentational with a reason.
    - `gui/tests/test_reverse_parity.py` walks the built windows and the CLI parser (the D-654 subprocess walk); it
      checks every key against the core schema and every command and option the registry names, including those
      quoted in its reasons. Non-vacuity floors guard the walk.
    - Every Settings pane is now `agentprov settings`: Jobs (`jobs.retention`, `retention_days`,
      `continue_on_failure`), Compute (`compute.*`, including the queue budget and `gate_n`), CI
      (`ci.default_target`), Dev runs and Estimate.
    - The CLI honours them: `jobs start` (queue budget), `jobs prune` (retention defaults), `batch create`
      (`--[no-]continue-on-failure` defaults to the setting). A corrupt settings file is refused with exit 2.
    - Gaps closed: `jobs follow --log` (the Logs page's records); the never-connected "Read repository variables"
      button was removed.
    - **User decision (2026-10-22, relayed by the orchestrator):** no migration of the values earlier GUI builds
      stored under the Qt keys `jobs/settings`, `compute/settings` and `ci/settings`; they read as the defaults.
  - **Rejected:** a GUI-only implementation with a parallel CLI (two implementations drift); a separate path package
    (one more project for no gain).

- **D-703 (2026-10-22, `agentprov settings`; part of D-700).**
  - **What.**
    - `agentprov.settings` keeps `$AGENTPROV_HOME/settings.json` (`agentprov-settings/0.1`, mode 0600): strict reads,
      atomic writes under a resource lock (read-modify-write).
    - A closed schema (key patterns with types, bounds, choices and validators) covers dev-run defaults and the live
      caps, estimate defaults, compute defaults (per-command `--jobs`, queueing, preset), job retention, and
      `endpoints.<name>.base_url`.
    - A local base URL must be http(s) on loopback or a literal private IP (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10,
      fc00::/7), with no host names, user info, query or fragment. The LAN opt-in stays per run (D-698).
    - An unknown key or a refused value is exit 2. A stored value that no longer validates reads as unset and is
      listed as ignored.
    - `get` returns `None` for an unset key; precedence (flag > environment > setting > registry) is the caller's.
  - **CLI:** `settings list [--prefix] [--schema] [--format]`, `get KEY`, `set KEY VALUE`, `unset KEY`. Values go to
    stdout.
  - **Rejected:** keeping them in Qt's QSettings (unreachable from the CLI); free-form keys (the file would gather
    arbitrary data); storing secrets (keys stay in the OS keychain, D-702).
  - **Tests:** `tests/cli/test_settings_cmd.py`. The CLI contract gains APP_COMMANDS.

- **D-710 (2026-10-22, RH-1 from the live Inspect harness; orchestrator ruling 2026-10-22, option (a); lands before the
  regeneration round; regeneration-batch item 168).**
  - **Finding.** Inspect writes `NaN` for an undefined metric: AgentHarm's `avg_score_non_refusals` is `NaN` when every
    sample was judged a refusal, which a small live pilot easily produces. The strict loader refused the whole
    `header.json`, so the log was one `select.dialect_planned` row with no execution. It was latent for the imported
    sources too; none of their stored logs hit it.
  - **Core (invariant 5; the reason is recorded in AGENTS.md).** `aer/locators.py`: the default `loads` of
    `LocatorResolver` is `strict_json_loads` with the `python-json` profile. It gives the strict profile's value for
    every document without a non-finite constant, and turns `NaN`/`Infinity`/`-Infinity` into `{"$float": ...}` (C.11.3)
    instead of failing the whole document. A locator pointing at such a value resolves to the object, never a
    number. This is a general hardening of untrusted parsing, not Inspect semantics. C.9.2 is amended.
  - **Adapter.** `dialect.load_header` parses with the same profile and tolerates non-finite numbers only under
    `/results` and `/stats`, which the mapper never reads. The units carry `header:nonfinite`, and the mapper reports the
    info issue `inspect.header_nonfinite`. The code is added to the `inspect` catalogue in place at version 2 (D-31
    owner: a shared catalogue changes in place until the round's first kept import records it). D.9.5 addendum.
  - **Rejected.** (b) A per-artefact loads hook threaded through `aer/validate.py`: more code for the same result.
    (c) Leaving the core alone: live pilots would need a non-refused sample in every log to import at all.
  - **Downstream.** The aer and the sem code digests of every family move, and so do the prov and validation digests
    (their closures include `aer/locators.py`), plus the `inspect` adapter digest and catalogue sha (pre-round review
    round 2a, R2-2: the first record left out sem). No AER, SEM or PROV byte
    of a stored corpus changes: every stored header parses strictly, the two profiles agree on such documents, and no
    `register.jsonl` under `~/.agentprov/{corpora,migration-work}` (54 files) records `ingest.number.nonfinite`.
  - **Round 2a follow-ups (2026-10-22, pre-round review of `inspect-rh1`; byte-neutral: 118,135 stored locators resolve
    identically, the AgentHarm re-map is byte-identical).**
    - R2-1: a `header.json` that is a bare non-finite constant raised `IndexError`. `load_header` refuses the root
      pointer with `ingest.number.nonfinite`, so the log stays `select.dialect_planned`, as before D-710.
    - R2-3: `strict_json_loads` gains `nonfinite_objects`, which collects the `{"$float": ...}` objects the
      `python-json` profile makes. `load_header` counts and places only those, by identity, so a literal one-key
      `{"$float": ...}` object in the source is ordinary data.
    - R2-4: the C.9.2 wording for pointers at and into the loader's `$float` object.

- **D-670–D-679 (2026-10-22, live `--defence` support; design note `docs/reports/defence-backends/design.md`; user
  decision 2026-10-22: every recommendation approved).** Built 2026-10-22: the class-0 harness and CLI on
  `claude/agentprov-defence-backends-538dc2` (lands after the rebuild window), the class-1 core on held
  `defence-backends-core` (lands after the round, regen-batch item 167); see the amendment at the end.
  - **D-670, architecture.** A defence registry `adapters/agentdojo/tables/live_defences.toml`, pinned by `{path, sha256}`
    from the live profiles. Provider kinds are `builtin`, `provisioned`, `port` and `fork`. The stock-built defended
    pipeline gets a tree rewrite with five delegating recorders (`prompt_wrapper`, `tool_list_filter`, `output_filter`,
    `executor_gate`, `aux_llm`) and a new harness hook `CaptureHooks.decision`. One defence per plan. `capture/0.1` is
    unchanged. The defence itself is the treatment (`task.defense_id`, actor `def0`, decisions, auxiliary calls), not
    instrumentation; only the harness's own effects are D.10.7 items (`agentdojo.defence_*@1`).
    **Rejected:** hand-built pipelines per defence; declaring the defence's effects as `request_modifying` (every
    defended session would fail NC-LIVE-01, and observer and treatment would blur); keeping defences import-only.
  - **D-671, first set.** AgentDojo 0.1.35's four built-ins (`repeat_user_prompt`, `spotlighting_with_delimiting`,
    `tool_filter`, `transformers_pi_detector`), Mandate (`mandate_envelope`, `mandate_scoped`, `mandate_intent`) and
    MELON (`melon`, `melon_at`, `melon_sm`, `melon_r`; `melon_rp` is absent at the pin and refused), all on the
    `agentdojo` backend. **Rejected:** built-ins only (it leaves the gate and auxiliary-call recorders unbuilt).
  - **D-672, downloads.** One consented fetch, logged in `acquisitions.jsonl`:
    - the `torch`, `transformers` and `numpy` wheels, in a new `defences` group of `backends/agentdojo` (a new locked
      environment);
    - `protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2` at a pinned revision with per-file sha256 (about 0.75 GB).

    Provisioned at build; offline at run (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`); CPU.
  - **D-673, allow verdicts.** Every verdict observed from a defence's verdict function (allow included) is recorded
    with label and score. An allow is never inferred from unchanged content.
  - **D-674, ports.** A patch only for recording or environment coupling, never for decision logic. Declared as
    `agentdojo.defence_port@1`: `behaviour_preserving` only if a differential test against the unpatched code passes;
    `harness_policy` or `request_modifying` otherwise. A new must-not-claim **NC-LIVE-03** forbids presenting a session
    with a port item as the authors' released implementation as run. MELON is the first port.
  - **D-675, defence endpoints.** `--defence-endpoint NAME`. Only that endpoint's key enters T2, and only when configured.
  - **D-676, copyleft defences** (aiAuthZ, Munim, gate, later llm-lock): deferred. Not in the first set; decide before
    the second set.
  - **D-677, placement and timing.**
    - The new rules go in a new `defence` catalogue (home under `adapters/agentdojo/rules/`), so imported corpora's
      catalogue digests do not move.
    - The class-1 core branch (the table, `agentdojo-live` and `autodojo-live` v2 with v1 archived, the four
      capture-mapper additions, fixtures) is held. It lands **after** the regeneration round, as a deliberate,
      recorded version bump (live profiles v2, the new catalogue at version 1). The round is not held for it.
      Corpora built in the round keep reproducing at their building commit (F-8 ruling), and `recompute` at main
      reports the moved agentdojo-family code digest as drift. The user first approved "before" in this session,
      then left the timing to the session, which chose "after" as relayed by the orchestrator (2026-10-22).
    - **Part 1 pre-round** (orchestrator, 2026-10-22; regen-batch item 167 part 1): the one `CATALOGUE_HOMES` line
      and the catalogue file land in the pre-round rebuild window, so every family's `aer` stage code digest moves once,
      before the round. Byte-neutral: nothing cites the catalogue until defended live sessions exist.
    - ROPE's placement (AutoDojo add-on or its own fork-pinned backend) is decided after its imports are read.
  - **D-678, weights.** `trust_remote_code` is refused. Gated weights need the user's acceptance of the model licence and
    an HF token at build time only, never in T2.
  - **D-679, exit code.** T0 checks a plan's defence before spawn, so a refused defence exits 5 from a plan as from the
    flag. (Today a plan exits 2 through `plan_refused`.)
  - **Byte classes.** Harness, CLI, locks and GUI are class 0. Everything under `adapters/agentdojo/` is class 1, held.
    No change to `aer/`, `prov/`, `validate/` or `corpus/` is expected (invariant 5), except the one `CATALOGUE_HOMES`
    line in `aer/rules.py` for the `defence` catalogue (invariant-5 note in AGENTS.md, as D-472 for `rescont`).
  - **Amendment (build, 2026-10-22).**
    - The registry is `backends/shared/src/agentprov_backend/defences.toml` (format `agentprov-defence-registry/0.1`,
      package data of the harness, class 0), not a core table: the worker reads the installed copy, T0 reads the
      repository copy and requires the two to be equal. The live profile carries only the allow-list
      `[family.agentdojo.live] defences`; each session records the registry digest and its entry.
    - D-672's download was done with the user's yes: the `defences` group of `backends/agentdojo` (torch 2.14.1,
      transformers 5.19.0, numpy 2.5.3) and `protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2` @ `90c9989b`
      (Apache-2.0, 8 files, 749 MB), each fetch in `acquisitions.jsonl`.
    - MELON: `melon`, `melon_sm` and `melon_at` run through the harness port `agentprov_backend/ports/melon.py`
      (D-674; client, call order, file writes, string content, MELON-AT state per cell). `melon_r` is not built: in
      recovery mode it inserts a system message at position 0 and replaces tool messages by copies, which the
      recorders cannot attribute without shifting positions.
    - D-675 is `run --defence-endpoint NAME`; provisioned code can also come from `backends build --defence-source
      DIR`, accepted only by sha256 and git blob id.

- **D-657 (2026-10-22, G5 signing; user decision relayed by the orchestrator).**
  - No Apple Developer ID will be bought, so Developer ID signing and notarisation are dropped from G5. The macOS
    bundle stays **signed ad hoc**.
  - **G5 exit criterion (macOS):** the ad-hoc-signed bundle starts on this Mac. On another Mac, the first launch
    needs Finder's right-click › Open (Gatekeeper); the README says so.
  - `gui/tools/build_bundle.py` signs nothing beyond ad hoc unless `--sign-identity NAME` is given (then that identity
    with the hardened runtime and a timestamp), so a real identity can be added later at no cost.
  - **Unchanged:** PySide6 6.12.1 when it reaches PyPI; Windows and Linux bundles on their own build hosts.
  - **Rejected:** a self-signed certificate (Gatekeeper treats it like ad hoc, and the trust step adds work); the Mac
    App Store (the sandbox blocks the checkout CLI, design §13).

- **D-664 (2026-10-22, kernel-enforced egress for sandbox-exec runs; user-approved with D-660 to D-669, design note
  `docs/reports/inspect-harness/design.md` §3.2; this entry is the record of what landed in the rebuild window; the
  D-660 to D-669 block arrives with the Inspect harness branch).**
  - **Containment.** The T2 profile denies every outbound connection except to two loopback ports given as parameters
    (`EGRESS_PORT`, `LOOPBACK_PORT`; G.4.10). For a remote endpoint both ports are T0's egress proxy
    (`cli/live/egress.py`). The proxy tunnels TLS through CONNECT, undecrypted, to the exact host and port pairs of
    the run's endpoints, forwards plain HTTP to a LAN model server's pair only (below), and refuses everything else.
    A loopback endpoint is reached directly through `LOOPBACK_PORT`.
    `PROFILE_SHA256` is `34018a40…`, so every environment re-probes once.
  - **Probe.** The probe checks:
    - the egress port: allowed;
    - `::1` on `LOOPBACK_PORT`: allowed;
    - another loopback port: denied;
    - `192.0.2.1:443`: denied.
  - **Transports.** The recording transports take the proxy from `AGENTPROV_EGRESS_PROXY`, through D-656's validating
    `egress_proxy()`. Without it they stay direct.
  - **Record (pre-round review R3-6).** The proxy writes its summary into the working manifest's `live` block as
    `live.egress`, or `null` when no proxy ran (scripted runs, loopback endpoints, operator-declared containment). Its
    shape is `{"kind": "connect_proxy", "allow": [<host:port>...], "tunnels": {<host:port>: <count>}, "forwards": {<host:port>: <count>}, "refused": {<kind>: <count>}, "refused_targets_distinct": <count>, "refused_targets_capped": <bool>}`.
    - `allow` and the `tunnels` keys are the pairs T0 itself put on the allowlist.
    - `refused` counts refusals per closed kind: `not_allowed`, `allowed_host_other_port`, `method`, `malformed`,
      `oversize`, `busy`.
    - `refused_targets_distinct` counts distinct refused targets with a BLAKE2b digest keyed per proxy and held in
      memory only. `refused_targets_capped` says that count saturated at 10,000.
    - No string the worker chose is ever recorded, and no digest of one (R1-7: a CONNECT target could otherwise carry
      a planted value past T0's fail-closed secret scan).
  - **Boundary.** `socket` is imported in `cli/live/` only by `egress.py`, which also holds the probe's loopback
    listeners (M.5.3).
  - **LAN forward mode (D-698 follow-up, 2026-10-22).** For a run with `--allow-lan-endpoint` and an `http://` base URL
    on a literal private address, `endpoint_target(..., allow_lan=True)` accepts the address (through
    `agentprov_capture.endpoints.is_private_lan_host`; IP literals join the allowlist in canonical form). The proxy
    then forwards plain-HTTP requests in absolute form, for that exact pair only:
    - methods `GET`, `POST`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`;
    - the request line rewritten to origin form, and `Host` regenerated from the pair (RFC 9112 3.2.2);
    - `Connection: close` in place of the hop-by-hop headers, and `Proxy-*` headers dropped;
    - the other headers passed as bytes, and the body as exactly its `Content-Length` bytes;
    - one request per connection: nothing after the body is read, and CONNECT to the pair is refused (LF-2).

    `live.egress.forwards` counts the forwards per pair. Every other request is refused with a closed kind:
    - `not_allowed` or `allowed_host_other_port`: a target off the list (or another port of a listed host);
    - `method`: another method, a request that is neither CONNECT nor an absolute-form forward, and CONNECT to a
      forward pair;
    - `malformed`: a head that does not parse, or is unsafe as below; a target with userinfo; a body framed other
      than by a single `Content-Length`;
    - `oversize`: a head over 8 KiB, or a body over 64 MiB;
    - `busy`: more than 64 open exchanges.

    An https LAN server is tunnelled through CONNECT, as any allowed pair; it is never a forward pair.
  - **Hardening before the first real LAN run (rebuild-window final re-check LF-1 to LF-5 and nits, 2026-10-22,
    class 0).**
    - **LF-1.** A head is refused (`malformed`) when a line holds a bare CR, LF or NUL, the method or a header name
      is not an RFC 9110 token (which also refuses folded lines and space before the colon), or the target is not
      visible ASCII. A bare LF had let a lenient server read a second, smuggled request.
    - **LF-2.** CONNECT to a forward pair is refused (`method`), so the forward rules cannot be bypassed through a
      raw tunnel. A forward passes exactly the `Content-Length` body; `Transfer-Encoding` and duplicate or malformed
      lengths are refused, and bytes after the body are never read.
    - **LF-3.** A malformed absolute form (a bad bracketed host, a bad port) is a `malformed` refusal, never an
      exception. Any unexpected error is counted the same way and logged nowhere, so no worker-chosen text reaches
      a traceback on T0's stderr.
    - **LF-4.** `stop()` cancels open exchanges before it waits for the server, with each step bounded (5 s).
      Before, a silent upstream held it for 30 s and left the exchange piping.
    - **LF-5.** G.4.10, the MN M.5.3 boundary table and this entry describe the forward mode.
    - **Nits.**
      - Brackets enclose an IPv6 literal only.
      - Zone ids are refused, and they fail `is_private_lan_host`.
      - An IP literal is an endpoint only on the LAN path (a remote https endpoint is named; an IPv4 literal had
        passed the name pattern by accident).
      - Schemes are compared in any case (`egress.forward_pairs`).
      - `Host` is regenerated from the pair (RFC 9112 3.2.2).
      - `provision_dataset` follows no symlink below the cache root or the environment.
  - **Class 0.** `cli/` is in no stage digest.

- **D-701 (2026-10-22, `agentprov prices` and `agentprov estimate`; part of D-700; user decision 2026-10-22: the shared
  code moves into the core).**
  - **What.**
    - The GUI's price, estimate, usage and priors modules move unchanged in behaviour to `agentprov.estimate`
      (`prices`, `cost`, `usage`, `priors`, `plan`). Their data moves to `src/agentprov/estimate/data/` (`prices.json`,
      `estimate_priors.json`, and a stand-in script). The builders move to `tools/estimate/`.
    - The format ids lose their `gui-` part: `agentprov-prices/0.1` and `agentprov-estimate-priors/0.1`. The shipped
      rows are unchanged.
    - Refreshed snapshots now live in `$AGENTPROV_HOME/prices/openrouter-<date>.json`, and overrides in
      `$AGENTPROV_HOME/prices/overrides.json` (`agentprov-price-overrides/0.1`, under a resource lock). Old GUI
      locations are not migrated; nothing had been released.
  - **`agentprov prices`:**
    - `list [--endpoint] [--format]` gives every endpoint's resolved prices (`agentprov-prices-list/0.1`).
    - `get ENDPOINT MODEL` gives the price one estimate would use, or nothing.
    - `set ENDPOINT MODEL --input --output [--cached-input] [--cache-write] [--as-of]` stores an override. A refused
      value is exit 2.
    - `unset ENDPOINT MODEL` removes one.
    - `refresh --allow-network` (exit 4 without it) or `refresh --from-file RESPONSE [--fetched DATE]` writes a dated
      snapshot.
    - The fetch goes through `agentprov.raw.fetch.UrllibTransport`, still the core's only `urllib.request` importer.
      It fetches one URL with no key, redirects only to `openrouter.ai`, needs HTTP 200 and accepts at most 16 MiB.
      The response is parsed strictly and keeps ids and prices only; its sha256 is recorded and the bytes are not
      kept.
  - **`agentprov estimate SOURCE <run options> [--stats-corpus DIR]… [--format text|json]`:**
    - It takes run's options less `ESTIMATE_OMITS` (the run-only outputs, preflight, consent, staging, conformance
      and the host-preset options); one `add_run_options` serves both commands, so new run options reach the
      estimate too.
    - It plans in-process with `run --dry-run --plan-json` and reads `run --catalogue` for tool-definition sizes
      (if that fails, it warns and goes on).
    - Cell statistics come from up to 16 `--stats-corpus` (200 sampled AER files each, counts only), else the
      shipped priors, else `settings` `estimate.default.*`. Prices come from `agentprov prices`.
    - A real model is planned with its key only with `--keychain`, `--env-stdin` or `--env-file`. Otherwise it uses
      the scripted stand-in and warns that settled units of a resumed real-model corpus are not subtracted.
    - The model id comes from `--model-id` only; `.env` is never read for it. Without one, the estimate shows no
      cost and says why.
    - The output is `agentprov-estimate/0.1`: plan summary, p50/p90/worst cost (decimal strings), calls, time,
      per-suite and per-attack groups, sources, warnings and the text lines. The text lines are the wording both
      forms print.
  - **GUI.**
    - Run Live calls `agentprov estimate … --format json` (with `--stats-corpus` for the open corpora and
      `--keychain` when allowed) and shows the CLI's lines and numbers. Model completion and the price line come
      from `prices list`.
    - Settings › Prices calls `prices list|set|unset`, and Settings › Estimate calls `settings list|set
      estimate.default.*`. Refresh model prices is the `prices refresh --allow-network` job (R2).
    - The GUI no longer holds price, priors or estimate code, `gui/tools/fetch_prices.py`, or the incoming-response
      import.
  - **Cost.** Each estimate spawns two backend workers (plan, catalogue): about 10 s warm on the scratch AutoDojo
    environment (28 s cold), against about 10 s for the dry run alone before.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a GUI-computed estimate beside a CLI one (two implementations);
    - `run --dry-run --estimate-json` (estimate is not a run mode, and its run-only options would need refusals);
    - keeping the overrides in `settings.json` (a closed scalar schema; overrides are records);
    - the stdlib-only fetch tool (a second network path in the core).
  - **Class 0.** `estimate/` and `cli/` are outside every stage closure. The shipped tables do not feed AER, SEM or
    PROV.
  - **Tests:**
    - `tests/estimate/test_estimate.py` (moved);
    - `tests/cli/test_prices_cmd.py` (fake transport, hostile response, refusals);
    - `tests/integration/test_estimate_cmd.py` (fake backend: scripted, stand-in, override, no price, usage errors);
    - `tests/boundary` (`estimate` at layer 2);
    - GUI `test_g3_live.py` (panes and dialog against a fake CLI) and `test_cli_parity.py`.
  - **With the live pilot (D-721, D-725, D-726; train-2 land 2026-10-22).**
    - The caps (`--max-calls`, `--max-cost-usd`, `--price-in`, `--price-out`) are **estimate options**, not omitted.
      A keyed dry plan of an API endpoint needs them (D-721 refuses an uncapped API run before any key is read), so
      `estimate` passes them through to its dry plan.
    - `estimate` also compares them with its numbers: a cap below the p90 cost or calls is a warning, because the run
      would stop starting cells at the cap.
    - The estimate's own prices (D-701) stay the source of its cost. `--price-in`/`--price-out` only price the run's
      cap.
    - `--i-consent-to-local-run` is in `ESTIMATE_OMITS`, with the API-cost consent: no estimate is a consent.

- **D-701 addendum (2026-10-22, follow-up: Anthropic snapshot ids; finding from the local-endpoints session's real list call).**
  - Anthropic's `/v1/models` serves dated snapshot ids (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`). Its pricing page prices models,
    which the shipped table keys by alias (`claude-haiku-4-5`).
  - `PriceBook.lookup("anthropic", id)` therefore uses the exact row first. Otherwise it strips a `-20YYMMDD` suffix
    and uses the alias's override or shipped row. `Price.model` stays the alias, and the note says "<id> priced as
    <alias>".
  - So a caller can tell which table row covers a listed id. `agentprov models` marks an alias as listed when a
    listed dated id resolves to it.
  - **Only Anthropic:** OpenAI prices some snapshots differently, so its dated ids are never priced by alias.
  - **Rejected:** copying dated ids into the table (it would go stale with each snapshot); a hand-kept alias map.
  - **Class 0.**

- **D-702 (2026-10-22, `agentprov keys` and `run --keychain`; part of D-700; user decision 2026-10-22: keyring becomes a
  core dependency).**
  - **What.**
    - `keyring` 25.7 joins the core's dependencies. It is locked offline from the uv cache (no download) and imported
      only by `agentprov/keys/helper.py` (M.5.3 row; a boundary test).
    - The helper is D-655's, moved from the GUI. It runs in a separate `python -I` process and constructs an
      allowlisted back-end directly (never `keyring.get_keyring()`). Its JSON protocol has the ops status, has, set,
      delete and emit.
    - `agentprov.keys` is its client.
    - `agentprov keys status|list|set|delete`:
      - only key variables `endpoints.toml` declares;
      - `list` shows names and presence only;
      - `set` reads the value from a no-echo prompt or `--stdin`, never argv, and registers it with the redaction first;
      - `delete` needs `--yes` when not interactive.
      - Without an allowed back-end: exit 4.
    - `run --keychain` reads the selected endpoint's key through the helper into the CLI process, which registers it
      for redaction at once. It is exclusive with `--env-file` and `--env-stdin`, and refused for a scripted run.
  - **GUI.** The GUI's own helper and keyring dependency are gone. Settings › Keys calls `agentprov keys`, and Run live
    passes `--keychain`, so the GUI never holds a stored key, not even in a pipe it opens.
  - **Rejected:** keeping keys GUI-only (the CLI could not manage them); `run` reading `keyring` in its own process
    (`jaraco.context` loads `urllib.request` into T0); keys in argv or the settings file.
  - **Class 0.** `keys/` and `cli/` are outside every stage closure.
  - **Tests:** `tests/cli/test_keys_cmd.py` (stub helper: names only, stdin only, refusals, `run --keychain` into the
    worker environment, exclusivity); `tests/cli/test_keys_helper.py` (the helper's protocol and import rules);
    `tests/boundary`.

- **D-702 amendment (2026-10-22, the default key source; user rule given in the local-endpoints window and confirmed
  by the orchestrator: "have the code look for the keychain first as the source of truth and if not then read the
  .env").**
  - `run` with none of `--keychain`, `--env-file` or `--env-stdin` takes the selected endpoint's key from the OS keychain
    first and falls back to the repository's `.env`. The other `.env` variables (model id, base URL, effort) are still
    read.
  - Each explicit option names one source only.
  - An unavailable keychain, or a missing entry, is a notice in the default mode. When neither source holds the key,
    the error names the variable and both places (exit 3), never a value.
  - `AGENTPROV_NO_KEYCHAIN=1` turns the keychain off for a process and its children. The test session sets it, so no
    test reads a developer's keychain.
  - `agentprov models` (D-730) follows the same order.
  - `estimate` is unchanged: it plans with a key only when given a source, else with the scripted stand-in.
  - **Why:** a worktree has no `.env`, and keys belong in the keychain.
  - **Rejected:** `.env` first (the keychain would be a fallback, against the rule); requiring `--keychain` (the
    default would stay `.env`).
  - **Tests:** `tests/cli/test_keys_cmd.py` covers keychain first, the `.env` fallback, neither source, an unavailable
    keychain, an explicit `--env-file` as the only source, and notices that name variables only.
  - **Order with the live pilot (train-2 land, 2026-10-22).** D-721's caps check comes first. A non-local endpoint
    entry without both caps is refused (exit 4) before any key source is read. That covers the keychain in the default
    mode and `--keychain` too: `--keychain` is checked for usage at the start but read only on the real-agent path,
    after the caps check. `--env-stdin` is still read first, because stdin is consumed before any other step (D-395).
    The test `test_an_uncapped_api_run_reads_no_key` covers both modes.
  - **Class 0.**

- **D-704 (2026-10-22, `agentprov jobs` and `agentprov batch`; part of D-700; user decisions 2026-10-22: the job
  manager moves into the core with `$AGENTPROV_HOME/jobs` and no migration, psutil becomes a core dependency, and a
  batch runs as a job).**
  - **What (jobs).**
    - `agentprov.jobs`: `record` and `follow` are read-only, and the GUI imports them (D-391 allowlist). `tiers`
      holds the R0/R1/R2 and destructive rules, moved from the GUI. `manager` and `supervisor` are the write side,
      reached only through the CLI.
    - A job runs `agentprov ARGV` in this interpreter (`-I`), or one `tools/<name>.py` of this checkout, under a
      detached supervisor (`python -I -m agentprov.jobs.supervisor DIR`, a new session). The supervisor records both
      processes' `(pid, create_time)` in `job.json`, passes a SIGTERM on, waits, and writes `ended.json` with the
      real exit code. The detached `jobs start` cannot wait, as the GUI did.
    - `--tool` must name a regular file inside the checkout's `tools/`: relative, no `..`, no drive, no symlink
      anywhere on the way, and resolved inside `tools/`. Nothing else can be started.
    - The rules at start are the GUI's (§4.4): one writer per corpus, either a running job or an `.agentprov.lock`;
      one job per slot (`network`, `backends`); and a job never starts jobs or batches (exit 4).
    - `stop` sends one SIGTERM to the CLI after the identity check (POSIX). `kill --yes` takes the supervisor's
      whole tree by process group after the identity check, waits up to 5 s, and records `how: killed`. `drain`
      writes the D-394 control file (`--with-control-file`), `resume` starts the recorded request again, and `prune`
      lists old ended jobs and deletes them only with `--yes`.
    - The child environment is the GUI's allowlist plus `AGENTPROV_NO_KEYCHAIN`. `job.json` records variable
      names only.
  - **What (batches; user decision: a batch runs as a job).**
    - `agentprov.jobs.batch` keeps `$AGENTPROV_HOME/batches/<id>.json` (`agentprov-batch/0.1`).
    - `batch create SPEC` (or `--stdin`) checks every step with the CLI's own parser. It refuses a step that starts jobs or
      batches, a destructive one (`purge` without `--dry-run`) and malformed fields (exit 2), and records the checkout
      pin (path, commit, digest of `git diff HEAD`; GR-70).
    - `batch start ID` launches one driver job, `agentprov batch run ID`, with a job id chosen beforehand and
      recorded in the batch under its lock. The driver ticks every 2 s (lock, load, advance, save) until every step
      has ended. On SIGTERM it stops (exit 130), and the steps it started keep running.
    - Each step is checked again before it starts, because the file is not trusted (GR-4): the parse, no recursion,
      not destructive, and no tier above the one recorded. A failure blocks the step with a fixed note.
    - R2 steps run only when the batch's `r2_confirmed_by` names this driver, meaning it was started or resumed with
      `--confirm-r2`. `start` without it refuses (exit 4). A later driver without it holds at the first R2 step and
      ends (GR-48).
    - A changed pin blocks every remaining step. Exit 4 or 70 blocks the rest unless `--continue-on-failure`. The
      dev-run fallback (D-529: a first-N import after `import.sample.unsupported`, or the part's later steps
      skipped) moves along.
    - **This replaces** the GUI design's "the queue advances only while the GUI is open" (research §Q2): no
      always-on service, one driver job per running batch, visible in Runs and stoppable like any job.
  - **GUI (part 3).**
    - The GUI's `JobManager` keeps its names but is a client. `spawn` runs `jobs start --format json` with the spec's
      corpora, slot, queue CPUs, progress level, `--tool`, notes and `--meta` facts (backend, call cap, dev-run part).
      Refusals come back with the CLI's code (`jobs.writer.busy` …), and a CLI that cannot run gives
      `gui.spawn.failed`.
    - `refresh` reads the job files through `agentprov.jobs.record`, and the `--meta` facts are merged into
      `record`. `stop`, `kill`, `request` (drain) and the prune listing are `jobs` calls.
    - The GUI refuses `--env-stdin` and `--env-file` in any job, because it holds no keys (D-702).
    - Batches are read from `$AGENTPROV_HOME/batches` and created, started, resumed and stopped through
      `agentprov batch`. There is no advance timer, and the GUI's batch rules and the dev-run fallback helpers are
      gone; the core applies them.
    - The GUI tests' fake CLI hands `jobs` and `batch` to the core's own CLI, with the job program replaced in that
      test process only. The real CLI has no option or variable that runs another program.
  - **psutil** is a core dependency (7.2.2, locked offline from the GUI's lock). Only `jobs/` may import it, and a
    boundary test proves the allowance admits psutil alone. psutil imports `socket` for constants (as D-545 for the
    GUI); no `jobs` module opens a socket. M.5.1 puts `jobs` at L1, M.5.3 gains the psutil row and the subprocess
    importers, and the reviewed subprocess list (SEC-11) gains `jobs/manager.py` and `jobs/supervisor.py`.
  - **Rejected:**
    - keeping the job manager in the GUI (the CLI could not start or control jobs);
    - a stdlib-only process identity (`ps`, `/proc` and ctypes per platform; user decision);
    - the GUI's `waitpid` (the starter exits, so it cannot wait);
    - `--tool` with any path (arbitrary command execution).
  - **Class 0.** `jobs/` and `cli/` are outside every stage closure: `regen_pins --affected` against 4d6a8d57
    names no family.
  - **Tests:** `tests/jobs/test_jobs.py` (supervised exit codes, the allowlisted environment, stop and kill, the
    writer, slot and lock rules, drain, resume, prune, no recursion, the `--tool` attacks: `..`, absolute paths,
    drives, symlinked files, directories and `tools/` itself; tiers); `tests/cli/test_jobs_cmd.py`;
    `tests/jobs/test_batch.py` (unknown, recursive and destructive steps, a step whose argv now needs R2, a tampered
    batch file, R2 confirmation, the pin, blocking exits, one driver job); `tests/boundary` (the psutil-only
    allowance); `tests/security/test_static_dangerous_calls.py`.
  - **Amendment (2026-10-22, F-14 from the user-guide session): relative paths mean the caller's cwd.** A job runs in
    its own folder, so `agentprov jobs start -- validate --corpus corpora/x` used to end with `corpus.missing`.
    `jobs start` and `batch create` now make every relative path option of the subcommand absolute against the
    caller's working directory before the spawn, and record it that way (`subcommand_argv`, `writes`, `reads`). Path
    options are those whose metavar names a path (`PATH`, `DIR`, `FILE`, `*.toml`, `*.json`, `ROLE=PATH`…), as
    `--opt VALUE` or `--opt=VALUE`; `-` and URLs are kept. Positionals are rewritten from the parser's metadata too
    (follow-up, same day): a path metavar always (`validate FILE…`), `inspect TARGET` only when it is a path (it
    exists under the cwd, has a separator, or starts with `.` or `~`), never an execution id. A `--tool`'s own
    arguments are not rewritten. Chosen over refusing them: a shell user's relative path then does
    what they mean, and the record is still unambiguous. The GUI already passes absolute paths, so nothing it starts
    changes. Tests: `tests/cli/test_jobs_cmd.py`, `tests/jobs/test_batch.py`.
- **D-705 (2026-10-22, `agentprov devrun`; part of D-700).**
  - **What.**
    - `agentprov.devrun.plan` holds the pure part, moved from the GUI: the settings (`agentprov settings` `devrun.*`,
      D-703), the part plan, the per-part summary and the run listing. It is read-only, and the GUI imports it for
      the Settings › Dev Runs preview and the Runs › Dev Runs table (D-391 allowlist).
    - `agentprov devrun plan|start|list|prune` (`cli/devrun.py`) does everything that writes:
      - `plan` gives the parts, sample counts and three steps per part, and writes nothing;
      - `start --confirm-r2` (exit 4 without it: the imports read the fetch cache) creates
        `dev-runs/<UTC stamp>/` and its `devrun.json` (`agentprov-devrun/0.1`), creates the batch (D-704,
        continue on failure, the checkout pin) and starts its driver job;
      - `start` then deletes all but the newest `devrun.keep` run folders, sparing every folder a running job or an
        unfinished batch uses (GR-25), and only real run folders, never a link (GR-26);
      - `list` gives the runs, newest first, with a summary per part;
      - `prune` lists old runs, and deletes them with `--yes`.
    - The steps are the GUI's (D-544, D-529):
      - `import --snapshot PART --fetch --sample N --sample-mode M [--seed S]` into `<run>/<part>`;
      - `validate`;
      - `recompute --dry-run`;

- **D-706 (2026-10-22, the Viewer's task and outcome columns and their CLI selectors; part of D-700; user request
  relayed by the local-endpoints session).**
  - **What the user asked.** Sort and filter a corpus's traces by suite, user task, attack, injection task, defence,
    model, utility and attack success; open a row's JSON and its rendered graph; highlight the rows whose attack
    succeeded, with a glyph as well as a tint (not colour alone), and nothing highlighted on an unknown or benign row.
  - **The rule for "attack succeeded".** An `outcome` element of the index row whose SEM claim is `attack_succeeded`
    holds (`holds: true`). The AgentDojo SEM profile gives that claim only on an attacked cell (`task.attack_id` a
    string) and only for a checker's result, never a harness default; a benign cell has no such element, so it reads
    "not judged" even when its raw security judgement is true. The GUI takes this from the row and computes nothing of
    its own. `utility` is the same rule with the claim `user_task_solved`.
  - **CLI selectors** (`agentprov stats --select`, `agentprov.api.iter_executions(select=…)`), so every Viewer filter
    is a CLI selection:
    - `cell.<member>`: a known H.7.4 cell member (`suite`, `task_id`, `attack_id`, `attack_target_id`, `defense_id`,
      `model`, `repeat`, …); an unknown member (`$unk`) never matches;
    - `outcome.<claim>=true|false|none`: an element with that claim holds, does not hold, or none has a `holds`;
    - `issue=<code>`: any of the row's issue codes.
    Working rows carry no cell or facets and match none of these (not even `none`). Class 0: `stats/` and `cli/` are
    outside every stage closure; no stored byte changes.
  - **The Viewer** (`gui/`): the columns suite, task, attack, injection task, defence, attack succeeded, utility,
    judgements and repeat; pickers for suite, attack, injection task, defence, model, utility and attack succeeded (yes,
    no, not judged); the `agentprov stats --select` line of the current filter with Copy CLI; the attack-succeeded rows
    tinted (theme- and contrast-aware) and marked with ⚑ plus "yes"; an Index Row tab; Export Graph… opens the
    `agentprov render --ex` job form. A working corpus shows a derive hint. The row readers live in
    `agentprov.corpus.rowvalues` (standard library only), which the GUI allowlist (D-391) now includes, so the GUI and
    `stats` share one implementation; a test checks that each filter selects exactly what its CLI selection selects.
  - **Rejected:** deriving "attack succeeded" in the GUI from the raw `security` judgement (it is true on the benign
    golden row, so it would highlight a benign trace); a GUI-only filter language (D-700: one implementation).

- **D-730..D-739 (2026-10-22, API providers' model lists; user requirement relayed by the orchestrator, the "auto once a
  day" choice the user's).** Models change often, so the picker must always offer a working list.
  - **D-730, the command.** `agentprov models --endpoint <openrouter|anthropic|openai|deepseek|gemini|llama|qwen|glm>`
    shows the provider's model list (`agentprov-provider-models/0.1`): from the dated cache by default; fetched now
    with `--allow-network` (R2). Endpoints: OpenRouter `GET /api/v1/models` (public; a key is sent only when given
    explicitly), Anthropic `GET /v1/models` (`x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, paged by `after_id`, at
    most 10 pages of 1000), OpenAI `GET /v1/models` and DeepSeek `GET /models` (Bearer key). `gemini`, `llama`, `qwen`
    and `glm` are OpenRouter shorthands: OpenRouter's list filtered by vendor prefix (`google/`, `meta-llama/`,
    `qwen/`, `z-ai/` + `thudm/`; a table in `cli/live/providermodels.py`, not `endpoints.toml`, so no env rebuild).
    List calls only: no tokens, no cost.
  - **D-731, network and data rules.** The registry host only (never a `.env` base URL); `http.client` over HTTPS with
    the default TLS context; no proxy; no redirect (only HTTP 200 counts); 20 s timeouts; 16 MiB per body; strict JSON
    through `agentprov.ingest`; checked members only (ids are labels; OpenRouter prices decimal strings). Keys never
    come from argv. **Order (user decision 2026-10-22): the OS keychain is the source of truth** (D-702); with no option
    the keychain is read first and the default `.env` only when the keychain holds no such key or cannot be read;
    `--keychain` reads only the keychain, `--env-file` / `--env-stdin` only those. The source used is a notice, never
    the value. Keys are registered for redaction before any request and travel only in their header; a keyed provider without a key is
    refused before any request (exit 3). **Rejected:** `urllib` (honours proxy variables); a key on argv.
  - **D-732, the cache.** `$AGENTPROV_HOME/models-cache/<endpoint>.json`, written atomically: endpoint, host,
    `fetched_at` (ISO UTC, this machine's clock at the fetch), each response's sha256, the rows (ids and metadata
    only). Shown with its date; `stale` after 24 h. A failed refresh shows the cached list with `refresh_error`; with
    no cache the list is empty (`source: "none"`); nothing is invented. A damaged cache is ignored, never half-read.
  - **D-733, auto refresh (the user's standing consent).** The setting `models.auto_refresh` (D-703 store; bool, off
    until the user switches it on). When on, `agentprov models --refresh-if-stale` (and the GUI's Run live, which
    calls it) fetches a configured provider's list when the cached one is older than 24 h, at most once a day.
    **Enabling it is the user's standing consent for these free list calls only** (no other network call, no model
    call, no cost). With the setting off, `--refresh-if-stale` only reads the cache and says so.
  - **D-734, run warning.** `run` with a provider endpoint reads that provider's cached list (no network): a requested
    model it does not list is a warning before the run, never a refusal (lists lag). The served model is still
    recorded and compared (A12).
  - **D-735, prices.** Each listed model carries `price_status` from the D-701 price table (`lookup`): `priced` or
    `no_price` (the estimate then needs a price override); priced models the provider no longer lists are reported as
    `not_listed` (`models_for` minus the price-table names the listed models are priced under: a dated Anthropic id
    priced by its alias, D-701 follow-up, covers that alias and carries `priced_as`). The CLI and the GUI read the same document.
  - **D-736:** its own entry (local model identity without load state). **D-737..D-739** reserved.
  - **Class 0** (cli/, formats, tests, the GUI's `models` form): no capture, backend, AER, SEM or PROV change.

- **D-736 (2026-10-22, a local model's identity leaves out load and serving state; finding from the live pilot's Part L;
  design approved by the orchestrator).**
  - **Finding.** On LM Studio, `identity_sha256` changed with the model's load state (same files: `671beca3…` unloaded,
    `95d6f4a5…` loaded), because `server_identity` held the loaded instance's `loaded_instances`, `parallel` and
    `context_length`. The identity feeds the configuration digest (D-693), so a run started cold and resumed warm
    would have been refused as mixed configuration (G5). The LM Studio server version was not recorded.
  - **Fix.** Per server kind, the native facts that describe load or serving state go to a new `observed_state` member,
    recorded but outside every identity digest (`localmodels.STATE_FIELDS`): LM Studio `loaded_instances`, `parallel`,
    `context_length` (the loaded instance's setting); llama.cpp `total_slots`. Ollama's `context_length` is the model's
    own and stays in `server_identity`. Ollama's `show_sha256` (a raw-response digest) leaves `server_identity`; the
    response stays cited in `listing.responses`. `identity_sha256` and the per-cell `server_side_sha256` (A14) now hash
    the same model facts.
  - **Server version.** `server.version` with a new `server.version_source`: Ollama `GET /api/version`, vLLM
    `GET /version`, llama.cpp `GET /props build_info` (moved from `server_identity`). LM Studio exposes no version over
    HTTP (checked on 0.4.23: `/api/v0/version` and `/api/v1/version` answer an error object), so its version is
    `null` with `version_source: "not exposed by the server"`, never guessed. LM Studio's own `/lmstudio-greeting`
    (`{"lmstudio": true}`) joins its fingerprint evidence when the server answers it. **Rejected:** the version from
    the macOS app bundle (Info.plist) or from running `lms version`: that is the installed application, not the running
    server's statement, it differs per OS, and `lms` would need a reviewed subprocess (SEC-11).
  - **Format.** `agentprov-local-model/0.2` (the member set changed: `observed_state`, `server.version_source`; state
    fields moved). D-31 criterion: a format recorded only in scratch corpora bumps rather than changing in place, so
    `agentprov-local-model/0.1` stays in `formats.py`, marked superseded. The live pilot's two Part L corpora carry 0.1
    records and the old (load-state-dependent) digest; they are finished and are not resumed.
  - **Class 0.** `cli/live/localmodels.py`, `formats.py`, the test stub and tests: no capture, backend, AER, SEM, PROV
    or validation change, no env rebuild, no stage digest moves (`regen_pins --check`). New local-model sessions carry
    the 0.2 record in their `agentdojo/local_model` note and in `live.local_models`, and their configuration digest
    differs from a 0.1-era run of the same model.
- **D-740 (2026-10-22, a per-cell call bound for Inspect cells under the D-725 caps; user-approved, option (a) of
  `docs/reports/inspect-harness/cell-bound.md`; class 0).** D-741 to D-749 are reserved with it; D-741 opens the
  `agentharm` · `live` gate, D-742 the Inspect preflight probe, D-743 the per-build Inspect model and errored-sample status, D-744 the probe in the caveat, and D-745 to D-749 are unused.
  - **Why.** D-725's worst case per cell is the AgentDojo cell's 48 calls. An Inspect cell is `cell_size` samples ×
    epochs, each with agent and judge calls, so capped Inspect runs were refused (D-667 addendum).
  - **Bound.** `n × E × ((M − 1) × (1 + a) + j) × (1 + K)` billed calls, from T0's own plan document:
    - at most `M − 1` agent calls per sample: Inspect 0.3.263 refuses a generate at the message limit;
    - `a` judge calls per agent call and `j` per sample, from the task's `InspectCallBound` in `cli/live/envs.py`
      `BACKEND_KINDS`. For AgentHarm `a = 1` (the refusal judge reads every assistant message) and `j = 3` (at most 3
      semantic-judge calls per grading function, none in a loop);
    - the bound is valid for the pinned code only (`task_files_sha256` `sha256:4ba500be…`, inspect_evals 0.20.0). The
      backend test re-derives `a`, `j` and the digest from the installed code;
    - `K = 1`: the worker sets Inspect's `max_retries=1` for the agent and every judge and turns the provider SDK's own
      retries off (`max_retries=0` model arg), because Inspect retries an empty 200 stream and timeouts, which D-725
      counts as billed. This is `inspect.harness_settings@2`.
  - **Refusals** (`cli.refused.api_caps`, exit 4):
    - a task without a bound, or with other task code;
    - a judge on another model than the agent (the caps have one price pair);
    - a plan without its message limit, epochs or cell size.
  - **Cells.** Under caps an Inspect plan defaults to `cell_size = 1`, so a cell reserves one sample's worst case and
    the recorded spend decides whether the next one starts. `Budget.cell_calls` replaces the constant in the start
    check and in `cap_bound_exceeded`, and `live.caps.cell_call_bound` records the bound used. AgentDojo-family runs
    are unchanged.
  - **The probe** (D-667, the user's typed yes on 2026-10-22, run after the round):
    - 4 AgentHarm samples, agent and judges gpt-4o-mini, `--max-cost-usd 0.50`;
    - `--cell-size 1`, `--message-limit 10`, `K = 1`;
    - each cell reserves 42 calls, about $0.305 at $0.15 in and $0.60 out per million tokens.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a token-limit-based USD bound for now (it needs a check of what Inspect counts against `token_limit`;
      cell-bound.md section 5);
    - per-role price flags (possible later if a judge model must differ).
- **D-741 (2026-10-23, `agentharm` · `live` promoted from `planned` to `partial`, pilot-style like D-720; the user's
  probe ordering relayed by the orchestrator on 2026-10-22, step 2; class 1, on the held `inspect-harness-core`,
  regeneration-batch item 170).**
  - **What.** The live part's gated value moves to `partial`. Under D.3.2, `partial` means "implemented for a declared
    subset of configurations", and the caveat names that subset:
    - OpenAI-chat endpoints only: the worker reaches the agent and every judge through Inspect's OpenAI-compatible

    - a local model server (loopback) with consent, or an API endpoint with consent and both caps (D-721, D-725,

    - under the caps, the D-740 cell bound: `--message-limit` required, every judge on the agent's model,
      `--cell-size` 1 by default, one retry per model call (`inspect.harness_settings@2`, which the `agentharm-live`
      profile now accepts in place of `@1`).
  - **Rule 3.** The caveat keeps "fake-client tested in v0.1; no real-model run" until the D-667 probe is recorded.
    Live corpora cannot be sealed in this build (`package.unsupported.live`), so no live part supports a "Live
    Capture" claim (U-18). The corpus is restricted-use and private (D-668).
  - **Gate.** The scripted D.3.2 live gate: the `inspect-agentharm` backend, the scripted end-to-end run through the
    worker (`tests/integration/test_run_live_inspect.py`: native-log session, index rows in mode `import`, validate
    and recompute with 0 differences), and the T0 identity, profile-pin and dataset checks (D-663).
  - **Rejected.**
    - Promoting it together with the three D-720 parts: those wait on their own pilot step (L-DY, B4); this part has
      its own probe and backend.
    - A `gated` status string: the vocabulary is closed (R-15).
    - Leaving it `planned` and lifting the gate for the probe alone: the status gate is the only switch `run` reads
      (N.2.1b(1)), and a one-off bypass would be an unrecorded exception.
- **D-742 (2026-10-23, the Inspect worker's own preflight probe; found by the first D-667 probe attempt; class 0).**
  - **Found.** The first real D-667 probe run stopped at preflight with exit 3 (`cli.environment.preflight`). The
    Inspect worker inherited the shared op `probe`, whose `runner.run_probe` imports `agentdojo.functions_runtime`
    before it builds a client. An Inspect environment has no `agentdojo`, so the worker raised `ModuleNotFoundError`
    before any HTTP request. No model call was made, nothing was charged and no corpus was written. Tests had missed
    it because a scripted run skips preflight, and no test ran `--preflight-only` through an Inspect worker.
  - **Fix.** `InspectWorker.op_probe` (`agentprov_backend_inspect.probe`) sends the D.10.9 request (the shared
    `PROBE_PROMPT` as the system message, `"Probe."`, the two probe tools) through the path a cell uses:
    - `models.build_model` (Inspect's OpenAI-compatible provider, `max_retries=1`, the SDK's own retries off);
    - the shared async recording transport and a `WireObserver` (`role: agent`), in its own capture session
      (`cell.task_id = "preflight_probe"`, artefacts `supporting`), with `inspect.preflight_probe@1` in its
      instrumentation and the note `inspect/preflight_result`.
    The results have the shared probe's shape and use its verdict functions (`roles_verdict`, the A4 text-call marks),
    so T0's A9, A3 and A4 rules apply unchanged.
  - **A3.** An Inspect cell transmits none of the agent's sampling parameters (its `GenerateConfig` sets
    `max_retries` only), so the probe configures none either: a configured `temperature` or the like shows as not
    transmitted, which is what a cell would do.
  - **Guards.** A backend test checks that `InspectWorker` overrides every shared `op_*`, so no shared op can run
    AgentDojo-family code in an Inspect environment. Scripted `--preflight-only` runs through the real worker are now
    tested for every live backend kind (agentdojo already; inspect-agentharm, autodojo and agentdyn added).
  - **Effects.** Class 0 (`backends/`, tests and docs): no stage digest moves. The installed
    `agentprov_backend_inspect` files change, so `inspect-agentharm-e3a9a78c` is rebuilt (same lock id) before the
    probe is re-run.
  - **Rejected.** Skipping preflight for Inspect backends: the probe is the only check of the endpoint's roles and
    tool calls before paid cells (D.10.9, D-291).
- **D-743 (2026-10-23, a new Inspect `Model` per build, and errored samples make a cell incomplete; found by the
  second D-667 probe run; class 0).**
  - **Found.** The second probe run (main `50cc806f`) exited 0 with 4 of 4 sessions sealed, but only sample `1-1` ran.
    `inspect_ai` 0.3.263 memoizes `get_model` on a key of model name, role, config, base URL, key and the JSON form of
    the model args, where the injected `http_client` maps to null. So:
    - the judges, on the agent's model in a capped run (D-740), got the agent's `Model`: their two requests in
      sample `1-1` are recorded in the wire log with `role: agent` under the agent actor. The `.eval` keeps them apart
      by scorer span, so the AER and the estimate's judge split (D-770) count 4 agent and 2 judge calls correctly;
    - cells 2 to 4 got cell 1's `Model`, whose capture session was closed: each sample ended with
      `CaptureLogError('capture log is closed')` before any request. Inspect's log status stayed `success`
      (`fail_on_error=False`), so the worker reported the cells `complete` and the run exited 0.

    The caps charged the 7 real calls (1 probe, 6 cell), with an upper bound of $0.051. The scripted tests had missed
    both: their judges use another model name, and each worker ran one cell.
  - **Fix.**
    - `models.build_model` calls `get_model(..., memoize=False)`, so every agent, judge and cell gets its own `Model`,
      client and observer. The header's `model_args` are unchanged (`memoize` is not a model arg).
    - A cell with an errored sample is `incomplete`, with a session note `inspect/samples_errored` `{count,
      sample_ids}`. T0 counts it inconclusive and the run exits 1, as for other inconclusive cells. The worker's
      `outcome` keeps its shape (`status`, `samples`, `samples_errored`).
  - **Tests.**
    - backend: distinct `Model`s and clients per build; two cells in one worker with judges on the agent's model, each
      complete, with every judge request `auxiliary` under a judge actor (this test fails with memoization on); an
      errored sample makes the cell `incomplete`, with the note;
    - end to end, in the probe's shape: every wire-log judge request is `auxiliary`, and the D-770 judge split read
      from the AER equals the wire log's judge requests; an errored sample gives exit 1 with both cells inconclusive.
  - **The second probe corpus** (`agentharm-live-probe-d667`, `migration-work`, not sealed) records sample `1-1`'s
    judge requests as the agent's in its wire log. Its wire log is never evidence of judge usage. Its AER and
    estimate counts are right, but its three errored samples are harness failures, not model behaviour, so the corpus
    is a debugging record only.
  - **Rejected.** Keying the memo by the client (Inspect's key is internal); retrying errored samples inside the
    worker (attempts are T0's, N.1.8).
  - **Effects.** Class 0 (`backends/`, tests and docs): no stage digest moves. The installed
    `agentprov_backend_inspect` files change, so `inspect-agentharm-e3a9a78c` is rebuilt before the next probe.
- **D-744 (2026-10-23, `agentharm` · `live`'s caveat records the D-667 probe, step 2 of D-722; class 1, held for the
  class-1 train).**
  - **What.** D.3.2 rule 3's phrase "fake-client tested in v0.1; no real-model run", which D-741 kept until the probe
    was recorded, is replaced by the probe's record: real-model probe 2026-10-23, approved by the user; API endpoint
    class; OpenRouter `openai/gpt-4o-mini` as the agent and both judges; 4 samples of the harmful split through
    `agentprov run`; working corpora, not sealed; restricted-use and private (D-668).
  - **Approval.** The user approved the probe results on 2026-10-23, in the Inspect harness session's window.
  - **Evidence.** `docs/reports/inspect-harness/probe-d667.md`: run 3 on main `68075b1d`, 4 of 4 conclusive, 25
    billed calls, about $0.003 used, judges recorded as judges, `validate --strict`, `recompute --dry-run` and the
    chain verification all pass. Runs 1 and 2 found D-742 and D-743. Run 2's corpus is a debugging record only.
  - **Scope.** The caveat names only what ran: one endpoint class (API), one model and four samples. The part stays

  - **Also.** The D.3.3 paragraph, the user guide's chapter 7 status box and the corpora table's row (README and
